President Donald Trump and two spokespersons lashed out Monday at Senator Jon Ossoff after he highlighted the 80-year-old Republican's relationship with a 35-year-old female aide.

Trump repeated his comparison of Ossoff to the iconic character created by the late comedian Paul Reubens when a reporter in the Oval Office asked about the Georgia Democrat's remarks, The Hill reported.

“You mean Pee-wee Herman?” Trump said.

White House communications director Steven Cheung got even more personal on social media, where he called Ossoff “Jon J***off” and “the biggest cuck loser in politics,” using a shortened form of the word cuckold, which is also a slang insult for a weak or submissive man.

“Jon should look deep into his soul and ask himself why he's a miserable person who hates this country. It's because he's a radical, extremist Dumocrat,” Cheung said, echoing his boss's favorite nickname for members of the opposing party.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump lashes out at Democratic Senator John Ossoff in the Oval Office ( AFP/Getty )

Another White House spokesperson, Davis Ingle, also joined in, calling Ossoff a “cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama.”

“Nobody gives a s*** what this lightweight loser says,” Ingle added on social media.

Ossoff's Senate office referred The Independent to his re-election campaign, which didn't immediately respond to an inquiry.

Recent polls have put Ossoff ahead of Republican challenger Rep. Mike Collins by anywhere from four to 13 percentage points in a race that the Cook Political Report rates “Lean Democrat.”

Senate Republicans now hold a 53-47 majority over Democrats and two independents who caucus with them, and Ossoff's re-election is widely considered crucial to Democratic hopes of wresting control from the GOP.

open image in gallery Ossoff says Trump ‘wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie,’ referring to White House aide Natalie Harp ( Getty )

During a Sunday campaign rally in Atlanta, Ossoff assailed Trump's war against Iran and said he “sleeps through his meetings, he golfs, and trades stocks.”

“He doesn’t want to do the job. He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar,” Ossoff added.

The “Natalie” he mentioned is White House aide Natalie Harp, 35, who was nicknamed the “human printer” by colleagues on Trump's 2024 campaign staff because she carried a portable, battery-powered device to make printouts for Trump, who prefers reading information on paper, The New York Times reported shortly after Trump's victory.

Harp, a former far-right cable TV host, has also written devotional letters to Trump, including one that said, “You are all that matters to me,” according to the NYT.

Harp’s estranged brother, Preston Harp, told The Daily Mail in June that her relationship with Trump was “very unhealthy,” and said she likely saw him “as a kind of father figure because he embodies the doctrine of American exceptionalism.”

Last month, Harp was among three White House aides who flew with Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth from Turkey to the U.K. on a military aircraft following a Nato summit, CNN reported last week.

Trump was snuck off Air Force One in a catering container in response to a reported Iranian assassination threat, as journalists and other administration officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, remained on the decoy flight.

Trump has claimed that “the plane that I flew on was at greater risk because that would be the plane I think that they would be more likely to go for,” even though he switched flights in secret.

During his second presidency, substantial personal wealth has remained a prized attribute for Donald Trump alongside political loyalty.

According to a report by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen, the Republican president has appointed more than four times as many people worth at least $100 million to his administration as the three previous presidents combined.

These figures for the Trump administration stand out compared to earlier administrations within the report from Public Citizen, published on Monday. In total, 57 Trump administration officials are worth at least $100 million, including 17 ambassadors alongside the remaining 40 serving in senior posts across the executive branch.

Eight of its 23 members fit the category, notably Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Education Secretary Linda McMahon, both billionaires ( Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz )

Look no further than Trump's Cabinet. Eight of its 23 members fit the category, notably Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Education Secretary Linda McMahon, both billionaires.

The president, himself a billionaire, has described his inclination toward appointing the ultra-wealthy as deference to financial success. And yet, Trump, who owes his White House comeback to support from middle-income, working Americans drawn to his pledge to lower everyday costs, now faces a midterm election electorate decidedly less keen on his handling of the economy.

Presidents have long sought counsel from the nation’s wealthiest people and tapped some for high-profile administrative leadership roles. Likewise, presidents routinely reward wealthy and influential supporters with ambassadorships.

Among the most notable examples is Andrew Mellon, the aluminum, oil and banking tycoon who was among the handful of the nation’s wealthiest people in the 1920s and served as treasury secretary for three presidents.

The Trump officials worth at least $100 million include Deputy Secretary of Defense Stephen Feinberg and Small Business Administration Administrator Kelly Loeffler, who are also billionaires, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and special envoy Steve Witkoff, both worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

By comparison, Republican George W. Bush’s administration and Democrat Joe Biden’s each included five members worth $100 million or more. Democrat Barack Obama’s included three, the report states.

A government populated by so many of the economic elite presents potential problems, the report's authors said.

"When the people holding the reins of government are drawn overwhelmingly from the ranks of the ultra-rich, it leads to misplaced incentives and corruption, and begs the question, ‘Whose interests they are truly serving?” said Lisa Gilbert, Public Citizen’s co-president.

The list does not include Trump, whose net worth Forbes estimates at more than $6 billion. Nor does it include space and social media giant Elon Musk, who advised Trump last year on an effort to reduce the federal government's size, scope and workforce and is the world's wealthiest person, with a net worth Forbes estimates at about $860 billion.

Trump's views are well established: Financial success is evidence of executive mastery and negotiating strength.

“They have great competence, those people. Incredible competence. Some of the smartest business leaders,” Trump said last year in explaining why he put considerable weight on advice from business executives.

He has also pointed to investments by wealthy people as a signal of future economic growth. To encourage billionaires to deliver, Trump, in his first year back in the White House, pursued policies on artificial intelligence and financial regulation that could benefit wealthy people, along with tax cuts and reduced regulatory burdens for large-scale investments.

Still, last month, only 32 percent of U.S. adults approved of Trump’s handling of the economy, down from 40 percent at the beginning of his second term and as his Republican Party faces headwinds in its attempt to hold both majorities in Congress in November.

Comedian John Oliver torched Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the “floating nightmare” on the USS Abraham Lincoln — after one sailor's mom said her son likened it to a scene out of the Fox TV show American Horror Story.

“Now, Pete Hegseth has claimed that the ship's conditions are being ‘completely misrepresented’ by those who are actually experiencing them, saying we make sure that every ship, every crew, every captain has everything we can provide at every single moment,” Oliver said Sunday on his HBO show, Last Week Tonight. “And if he means to go certifiably insane, I'm inclined to agree with him there.”

He added: “You never want to be in a position where you describe your job as a scene out of American Horror Story.”

“Honestly, if you absolutely have to choose a Ryan Murphy show for your workplace to resemble, the obvious answer is All's Fair,” he said, referring to the creator's Hulu drama about an all-female law firm. “Yeah, that's the Ryan Murphy production you're going to want to be stuck in, not this floating f****** nightmare.”

In response to an inquiry from The Independent, a Pentagon spokesperson declined Monday to address Oliver's remarks and instead referred back to Hegseth's assertions Friday.

open image in gallery HBO host John Oliver mocks Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s response to concerns over conditions on the USS Abraham Lincoln ( Last Week Tonight with John Oliver/HBO )

Last week, military mother Danielle Rappa told NBC News that her son, who's aboard the Lincoln, was initially “in good spirits” but that his mental health had “started getting very dark,” during extended combat operations in President Donald Trump's war against Iran.

“He describes the overall experience as a scene out of the American Horror Story, where he feels like everybody is dead but they don't know it yet,” she said.

In a prepared statement, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told The Independent, “The President cares about our troops more than anyone, and he is ensuring our brave servicemembers have all the resources they need to be successful as the United States Military continues to economically strangle the Iranian regime.”

The Lincoln —a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier with a crew of more than 5,000 sailors and Marines — left its home port of San Diego on November 21 and has since set a record of more than 240 uninterrupted days at sea, according to The Associated Press.

The USS George Washington is en route from Asia to replace the Lincoln as one of two aircraft carriers stationed in the Middle East, according to reports.

The Lincoln's deployment was supposed to end in May, and deteriorating conditions on board —including reported food shortages, broken toilets and moldy showers — have caused morale to plummet, according to family members.

open image in gallery Relatives say morale is plummeting due to deteriorating conditions amid the Lincoln’s record-setting deployment ( Reuters )

Last week, CNN reported that a sailor had jumped overboard August 3 and was rescued about an hour later following what a Navy official described as a mental health episode. Multiple others have also tried to jump off the ship but were stopped by fellow crew members, relatives told the Military Times.

On Friday, Trump sparked outrage after being asked by a reporter whether the Lincoln's deployment had gone on too long.

“No, not nearly enough,” Trump said.

Karen Bramlett, whose grandson is serving on the Lincoln, told NPR that he's "depressed" and that his dreams about Navy service "have been shattered" by his time on the ship.

“Donald Trump needs to be ashamed of himself to let them suffer the way that they're doing,” she said. “They're over there fighting for our country. And this is the thanks they get? They can't even get help from him or his administration.”

The second largest reservoir in the U.S. just hit its lowest point on record as drought continues to plague the dwindling Colorado River.

Lake Powell — located between northern Arizona and southern Utah — had fallen to 3,519.8 feet as of Sunday, according to data from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation. On Saturday, the lake's water level dropped down past its previous low record, which was set in April 2023, The Hill reports.

The water in the lake is 3.8 feet lower than it was a month ago, according to USBR data.

It's not the only major reservoir facing historic depletion. The water level in Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the U.S. and also fed by the Colorado River, has dropped more than 23 feet since the start of the year. As of Monday, its elevation is 1,039.83 feet, a record low.

Last month, the USBR projected that Lake Mead's water level will fall below 1,110 feet by July 2028, which is nearly 120 feet below its benchmark for a "full pool," according to the agency.

open image in gallery Water levels in Lake Powell, America’s second-largest reservoir, fell to historically low levels in August ( Getty )

The Colorado River and the pair of reservoirs are critical for seven states — Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming — as all rely on it for their water supplies. That includes hydropower production, recreation, fishing, wildlife, and agriculture.

Approximately 35 to 40 million people rely on the river and the reservoirs for their water.

The depletion of the Colorado River and the bodies it feeds is not a new problem; the river has been in a drought state for more than 25 years. Human-driven climate change and heavy use have only exacerbated the issue over the years.

Last month, the Department of the Interior released an Environmental Impact Report calling for the three Lower Basin states — Arizona, California, and Nevada — to adhere to strict new water management framework. The new rules will call for a mandatory water-use reduction of 3 million acre-feet annually through 2036.

open image in gallery Tourists on the Hoover Dam look out at the bathtub ring of minerals that shows the former water levels of Lake Mead near Boulder City, Nevada

The new framework is facing opposition by some leaders from the Lower Basin states, including Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs, who said the report “contains unacceptable options that include the federal government forcing Arizona to take the majority of draconian water cutbacks.”

"Inequitable, federally imposed cuts to our Colorado River water allocation will be unacceptable to Arizonans, and will put every American at risk," she wrote in a statement following the release of the framework. "Previous federal proposals to slash Arizona’s Colorado River water would be devastating for our nation as we work to compete with China in the AI race, onshore critical supply chains, feed the country, and rebuild our depleted missile stockpile."

The new plan will replace a 2007 framework that expires in the fall, according to the paper.

“This framework provides the flexibility to respond to changing hydrologic conditions while preserving the opportunity for the Basin States to continue working toward durable, consensus-based solutions,” Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum said in a press release last month.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five key budget enablers
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.

Telegraph Fantasy Football managers need to make compromises to fit in fantasy heavyweights like Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Bruno Fernandes (6.5m). Picking some set-and-forget budget enablers who have either high point ceiling potential or will return a steady stream of points, is key to freeing up those funds.

Below are five players the Fantasy Football Hub experts have highlighted for consideration.





Brian Brobbey (£3.3m)

The Sunderland forward had a steady Premier League debut season, netting seven times and helping the Black Cats qualify for the Europa League. The Dutch international netted three times at the World Cup, improving his stock further, and will be looking to get off to a goal-scoring start against Ipswich and Fulham in GWs 1 and 2.



Enzo Le Fee (£3.3m)

Depending on the formation TFF managers are using, Brobbey’s midfield teammate at the same price may be the preferred route to target those opening fixtures. The 26-year-old accrued 12 attacking returns last season, and bumped up his overall score with an impressive 93 tackles.



Harry Wilson (£3.2m)

The midfielder swapped London for Yorkshire in the summer, as he looks to expand on a whopping 17 attacking returns from last season. Feeding the rejuvenated Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.9m), and adding goals from midfield for Leeds will be two primary objectives for the Welsh international, who could make a mockery of his mere marginal price increase.



James Trafford (£3.0m)

Another Leeds United summer acquisition, Daniel Farke fought off rival Premier League suitors to land the ex-Manchester City shot-stopper. Leeds United have a mixed bag in terms of opening fixture difficulty, but do have three home league games in the first five before the international break, and the new no.1 has an outside chance of getting the nod in the Carabao Cup games too, so there are points available should the Whites be able to shut out the opposition.



James Hill (£2.6m)

If looking to fit in more big-hitters, a sub £3m player can be extremely useful for team balance, and the Bournemouth defender looks assured of starting having played a pivotal role in getting the Cherries into Europe this season.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five essential players for the 2026/27 season
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub, will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount.

Five best fantasy football players





Take a look at these elite Telegraph Fantasy Football tips below:



Erling Haaland (£8.3m)

Comfortably last season’s top points scorer with 254, the Norwegian striker will once again likely be the first name in TFF Managers’ XIs. Having come back late from his post-World Cup break, there may be nervousness about early-season minutes. However, if he keeps up his phenomenal August goals-to-games ratio, starting without him may mean playing catch-up against the field.



João Pedro (£5.1m)

Having missed out on the Brazilian squad for the World Cup, the forward looks rejuvenated after a rested summer, netting seven times and assisting twice more in pre-season. With no European distractions for the Blues this season, and attacking intent shown in new manager Xabi Alonso’s selections thus far, the 24-year-old looks primed for a successful season.



Antoine Semenyo (£4.9m)

Perhaps one of the biggest surprises in the pricing for the new season was the City winger’s sub-£5m tag. The January recruit was the second-highest scorer in the game last season, and has looked the most dangerous of Enzo Moresca’s attacking assets in pre-season, so looks the stand-out midfield option.



Gabriel Magalhães (£4.9m)

Another that perhaps warranted a higher price increase, the Brazilian only missed out on breaking the 200-point barrier due to his injury late in the season. While there are cheaper options in the champions’ backline, including Christhian Mosquera (£3.7m), who looks likely to deputise for the injured William Saliba (£4.6m), getting the assurances over long-term starts and the additional attacking returns is enough to warrant paying the higher expense.



Nico O’Reilly (£4.2m)

The England international has incurred a position change in TFF, and will now gain points for clean sheets as a defender on top of his attacking returns. Had he scored as a defender last season, he would have topped his position table; therefore, £4.2m seems too good value to turn down.



One notable omission from the list is Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m). It isn’t through the belief that the veteran won’t return heavily once again this season, but rather that there appears to be more value across a wide range of mid-priced options where TFF managers can optimise value across their starting XIs.

News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

News.title: How to have the perfect slow-paced holiday in Zakynthos
News.content:
Zakynthos, also known as Zante, is renowned for raucous nightlife, but there’s a far more authentic side to the Venetians “Fiore di Levante” (Flower of the East). For such a small island, scenery is extremely varied: the southern coastline – home to Laganas’ notorious nightlife strip – also encompasses the pristine beaches of Zakynthos Marine Park, where loggerhead sea turtles come to nest, while some of the island’s best-known attractions, including Navagio Beach on the cliff-lined northerly coast, can only be reached by boat.

Birthplace of the man who penned Greece’s national anthem, Zakynthos was also a magnet for literary greats: Byron lay in state here and philhellene Edgar Allan Poe wrote a sonnet to the island’s “verdant slopes”.

Last but not least, food is a powerful lure here: sit in a rustic sea view tavern sipping local Verdea white wine with a plate full of traditional kouneli stifado – a garlic and tomato-soaked rabbit stew – and you’ll be hooked.

Sports.title: Watch furious Jack Wilshere’s sweary dressing room rant as Arsenal hero inspires Luton to 4-3 win from 3-1 down
Sports.content:
FOOTAGE of Luton manager Jack Wilshere in a fit of fury has appeared, as he attempted to gee up his team while they were 3-1 down at half-time at the weekend.

Wilshere‘s side went on to spectacularly win 4-3 in their League One opener away at Reading.



It was assistant manager Chris Powell who teed up gaffer Wilshere to start with.

He said: “Let me tell ya, let me tell ya, you f***in can come back in this, alright, whatever the gaffer says, we’ll f***in take it on board.”



And Powell was pretty much bang on.

Wilshere said: “The truth is boys I must be f***in going crazy, but I spent six f***in weeks telling you we dropped points against counter-attacking teams.

“What happens on day one? We concede three goals, three goals, we give them a hat-trick, a f***in hat-trick lads.”

It was EFL journeyman Jack Marriott who bagged a 30 minute hat-trick for the Royals.

Wilshere continued: “Come on please, we can do all we want, but if we ain’t f***in there in duels, if we don’t land on second balls, it doesn’t matter.

“Be clean, be clean please! We do passing drill after passing drill, where it goes bang, bang opposite side.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“It’s for now! It’s for now lads! This is where it matters!

“Lads it’s still there for us, it’s still there, we can go and score two in ten minutes and we can f***in kill them.”

And the Hatters’ response was even better than that, as they scored two in two minutes.

Kasey Palmer’s 50th and 52nd minute goals restored all order for Luton and Wilshere.



And the Luton players gave their gaffer the dream ending, as they dramatically nicked all three points in the 97th minute.

Gideon Kodua bagged the winner in his first appearance since signing for the Hatters permanently, after spending last season on loan at Kenilworth Road.

Sports.title: Man Utd in talks with Bruno Fernandes over new contract after Galatasaray him offer staggering £350,000-a-week deal
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes after their skipper received a mega proposal from Galatasaray.

The Turkish champions offered the 31-year-old midfielder around £18.3million-a-year tax free, but Fernandes wants to remain at Old Trafford.



United have entered preliminary talks with the Portugal star who has entered the final year of his current contract, which has the option of an additional 12 months.

Well-placed sources say there is no rush to get the deal over the line but talks have been discussed.



Fernandes signed his current deal in 2024 and his £57m release clause for overseas clubs expired last month.

United plan to reject any offer for Fernandes and have not received any concrete contact over the Prem Player of the Season.



Galatasaray were intending to table around a £42.8m offer for Fernandes, who turns 32 next month.

Galatasaray president Dursun Ozbek has been overseeing the audacious bid and is determined to sign Fernandes.

The Turkish giants are understood to be willing to give the United captain a four-year contract worth £18.3m annually, plus a further £3m up-front signing-on bonus.

Turkey’s tax system means Fernandes could double his current take-home pay if he made the switch.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandes, who has also been linked with Juventus and AC Milan this summer, has previously turned down eye-watering offers from Saudi Arabia.

Fernandes revealed he was “hurt” in October when he felt Ineos chiefs wanted to cash in on Al Hilal‘s £100m enquiry last summer.

The Saudi Pro League club were willing to double Fernandes’ wages up to £700,000-per-week.

The playmaker credited ex-manager Ruben Amorim for playing a role in convincing him to stay at Old Trafford, to see if the club could match his ambitions.

Fernandes played a major role in securing Champions League football this season, but United have spent just £85m on two new signings in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced to change 2026/27 third kit for Champions League clashes as club release explanation
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have explained why they have been forced to make a change to their third kit’s design in the Champions League.

The Red Devils are back in Europe’s premiere competition for the first time in three years, meaning this will be the club’s first under the Swiss-league style format introduced in the 2024/25 season.



Michael Carrick‘s team will find out who they will face when the fixture list is drawn on August 26.

However, Man Utd have already been forced into making one alteration from their domestic plans because of their third kit.



The club’s new third kit was released on Friday with three central logos of the famous devil crest, Snapdragon fireball and adidas‘ three-stripe emblem.

This design was agreed between all parties to mark a fresh style and clean look unique for this season.

But a club statement has also revealed why the Snapdragon symbol will NOT be present on their shirts when they use it in the Champions League.

It said: “The Reds are due to sport the jersey when required across domestic competition this term, although UEFA rules mean that the ‘Snapdragon’ wordmark will be added to our players’ shirts for any Champions League matches it is worn in.

“This is because the same version of a logo must be used across all of a club’s kits in the tournament, so the sponsor on the third strip needs to match that on our new home and away releases, which feature the wordmark.”

Snapdragon have been Man Utd’s front-of-shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024/25 campaign.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The club’s kits will also be manufactured by adidas until 2033 after signing a 10-year extension in 2023 worth a minimum of £900million.

Earlier this month they signed a deal with Betway as a training kit sponsor worth £20m a season.

Carrick’s side will kick off their Premier League season with an away trip to newly-promoted Hull on Saturday.

They then host fellow promoted club Ipswich at Old Trafford the following Sunday.

Sports.title: Why Jack Grealish was in stands for Cardiff vs Wrexham clash more than 24 hours after unhappy Man City return
Sports.content:
JACK GREALISH was seen in attendance of the Welsh derby between Wrexham and Cardiff.

The England and Manchester City star was spotted in the crowd a day after his club’s 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Arsenal in the Community Shield.



That game was actually played in Cardiff’s Millennium Stadium, a mere stone’s throw away from Cardiff City Stadium.

And with no Man City game to worry about until their Premier League opener at the Etihad against Bournemouth next Sunday, Grealish opted to remain behind to watch the derby game.



The 30-year-old was picked up by Sky Sports cameras watching the two Championship sides clash.

It turned out he was in the stands to support best mate and Bluebirds star Callum Robinson.



Robinson, 31, is a childhood friend of Grealish, and both played in the academy at Aston Villa.

The pair have remained close, and were seen on holiday together over the summer.

Unfortunately for Grealish he had to wait to see Robinson in action as he was named on the bench to start the game.

But the forward eventually came off the bench in the 79th minute as Cardiff scored a last-gasp equaliser to draw the game 1-1.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Grealish was resigned to the same fate against Arsenal, coming off the bench at half-time with the Premier League champions already 2-0 ahead.

However, he was unable to help inspire a similar comeback.

New City boss Enzo Maresca opened the door for Grealish to become an integral part of the team again, with the winger having fallen out of favour under former boss Pep Guardiola.

Maresca said: “Jack was inside when we were 2-0 down so the game already became complicated after that, but overall I think Jack was good.



“The ones that are still here and want to work every day and if they deserve they’re going to get minutes.

“At the moment the transfer window is open and we will see what happens.”

Grealish spent last season on loan at Premier League side Everton.

He enjoyed a bright start to life under David Moyes as he registered four assists in his opening three games, but only managed a two more all season while also chipping in with match-winning goals against Crystal Palace and Bournemouth before a foot injury ended his season in January.

The former Aston Villa talisman has not featured for the England national team since 2024.

He is in the final year of his contract at the Etihad, where he has won three Premier League titles, the FA Cup, Champions League and Club World Cup.

Sports.title: Mike Bailey dead at 84: Former England star and legendary Wolves captain dies as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
WOLVES legend Mike Bailey has passed away at the age of 84.

The ex-midfielder who played for England on two occasions, spent 11 years at Molineux.



In their official statement, Wolves described Bailey as the club’s leader during their revival in English football in the 60s and 70s.

It read: “During that popular Wolves stint, Bailey was known by those on the Molineux terraces for his love of a tackle, creative passing and eye for the occasional spectacular strike, but more than all that, his leadership.”



During his first full season at the club, Bailey was part of the side who won promotion back to the top division in 1967.

He was named Midlands Player of the Year in the process.



Once Wolves were back in the big time, Bailey was a key figure in the team who reached the Uefa Cup final in 1972.

They lost 3-2 to Tottenham Hotspur in an all-English affair.

Bailey was then able to get his hands on some silverware two years later, as he captained Wolves to a League Cup triumph at the Old Wembley.

In what the club described as his “finest afternoon at the club”, Wolves came out 2-1 winners over Manchester City.



It’s also worth noting that Bailey’s impressive career saw him make two national team appearances in 1964.

Following his retirement from the game in 1979, after a season in America with Minnesota Kicks and one last campaign with Hereford, Bailey went on to manage Hereford, Charlton, Brighton, Greek team OFI and Leatherhead.

After being diagnosed with dementia in 2020, Bailey died today at the age of 84.

The tributes have poured in for the legend.

One fan wrote: “Rest well captain.”



Another said: “So sorry to hear of the passing of Mike Bailey. Just before my time supporting Wolves.

“But everyone tells me he was as tough as they came and an inspirational leader. Thoughts with his family and friends.”

While a third posted: “Just hearing the very Sad news of the passing of the Great Mike Bailey sending my Deepest Condolences to his Family and friends at this sad time

Charlton Athletic also posted: “We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player and promotion-winning Manager Mike Bailey at the age of 84.”

Sports.title: Cole Palmer reveals he gave himself food poisoning the last time he cooked – and admits he has no idea how
Sports.content:
CHELSEA star Cole Palmer has revealed he poisoned himself by botching his cooking of a salmon dish.

The England ace, who has a reputation as one of football’s funniest characters, admitted: “I’ve not cooked for ages, to be fair.



“The last time I cooked I gave myself food poisoning . . . salmon.

“I don’t even know how you get it from that, but the doc said it was that.”



He added: “I had a few cooking lessons, but it’s not for me.”

Palmer has switched his attention to business.

The Manchester-born star, dubbed Cold Palmer due to his trademark shivering goal celebration, has launched his own purified ice brand, Cole’d Ice.

He said: “When I’m not playing, it’s something else to think about. It’s healthy and something to give back to the fans.”

Palmer, 24, also laughed off his comic reputation. He told i-D magazine: “I just think it’s funny because people always say to me, ‘He’s so funny, he’s so this’.

“But it’s just normal, I’m just doing normal things.”



He went viral last year for a deadpan interaction where he asked a waiter at a posh restaurant if he made the food himself, then requesting ketchup.

Supporters begged the ­Chelsea hero to “never change”.

Many were furious when he was left out of England’s World Cup squad, but he hopes to rejoin Thomas Tuchel’s Three Lions set-up next month.

Sports.title: Sky Sports and TNT Sports allowed to air never-before-seen feature in major Premier League broadcasting change
Sports.content:
AUDIO of on-field conversations between Premier League referees and players will be heard during live broadcasts for the first time this season.

Howard Webb, chief refereeing officer for Pro Ref (formerly PGMOL), has pushed for greater transparency on decision-making since his appointment four years ago.



Webb created the ‘Mic’d Up’ programme in 2023 to help show how key calls are made by officials.

The latest step in enhancing coverage and understanding for spectators will be for one or two clips to be shown from the head-mounted RefCams worn by officials during each match round.



Premier League domestic right-holders Sky Sports and TNT Sports, will have the right to show the footage in their broadcasts.

Previously, RefCam footage could only be televised several days after matches.



But those regulations will be relaxed in the 2026-27 campaign.

Rules put in place by the International Football Association Board (Ifab) mean no audio can be broadcast live concerning incidents referred to Video Assistant Referee.

But one or two instances from each match round can now be shown by Sky Sports and TNT Sports during matches.

While it understandably can’t be broadcast live, the difference is Sky and TNT can show footage from incidents during the game, instead of days later.

Sports.title: Sheff Utd facing 12-POINT deduction, claims former owner, sparking furious response from club bosses
Sports.content:
SHEFFIELD UNITED’S owners have hit back angrily at former chief Prince Abdullah after claims the club faces an EFL 12-point penalty.

Sources close to current bosses Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen slammed the ex-owner’s latest move as a clear “publicity stunt.”



The fiery response follows claims from Abdullah’s camp that a winding-up petition against the Championship club’s former holding company could trigger docked points.

United World, Abdullah’s investment firm, claims it is still owed £35million from the club’s 2024 takeover deal.



A winding-up petition is a legal court action creditors use to force a company into liquidation to recover unpaid debts.

They claim if the former parent firm is wound up this week, the Blades face the real prospect of a sanction.



Football finance experts warn a winding-up order could trigger the EFL‘s “two insolvency strikes and you’re out” rule.

Under EFL regulations, an insolvency event at group level carries an automatic 12-point penalty.

It could also disqualify co-owners Rosen or Eltoukhy under the league’s strict owners’ and directors’ test.

In a full statement, a source close to the owners said: “We are disappointed Prince Abdullah is trying to hurt the club and its supporters with publicity stunts.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The deal between sophisticated parties in 2024 was well advised by his financial advisors.

“Sheffield United is financially healthy, unlike under Prince Abdullah when the club incurred a points deduction for missing payments to football creditors.

“Nonetheless, Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen invited Abdullah to re-invest in the Club and join the ownership of Sheffield United and to help use his skills to support our promotion efforts.

“Helmy and Steve are focused on the sustainability of the club and the season ahead.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president

FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, said that he and his colleagues had been 'deceived' by Gianni Infantino's now scrapped plan to sell the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino continues to receive backlash (Image: Jared C. Tilton - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA has sacked its chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, after he criticised president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off the World Cup. Lamour, a longtime colleague of Infantino at both FIFA and UEFA, said that staff had been 'deceived' by the plan which has now been scrapped following widespread backlash.

‌



Sky News first reported Lamour's departure. While FIFA chose not to comment on the nature of his exit, football's world governing body did offer a statement.

‌



"FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA's Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026," the statement read. "FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future."

‌



A letter sent by FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom has also surfaced. It informed FIFA staff about Lamour's departure, with the Frenchman having been with the organisation since November 2024.

"Kevin joined FIFA in November 2024 and in this time has overseen a period of significant change, including improved relationships with stakeholders and the delivery of several significant projects of joint interest, amongst many other key achievements.

"You will have seen Kevin present in each FIFA Council meeting since his appointment in 2024, and many of you will have had a regular working relationship with Kevin on projects of various kinds since his joining FIFA.

I wish Kevin all the best for the future." Last month, Lamour made headlines by saying that he and his colleagues were 'deceived' by Infantino's plan to sell FIFA competitions, including the men's World Cup to private investors, labelling it 'the project of one person'. The 45-year-old also suggested that the under-fire president should step down from the position which he's held since 2016.

Sports.title: Liverpool star accused of 'white lie' as he tries to force through summer transfer
Sports.content:
Liverpool star accused of 'white lie' as he tries to force through summer transfer

There are just two weeks left in the summer transfer window and Liverpool are close to agreeing a deal to sell midfielder Curtis Jones to Inter Milan following prolonged negotiations

View 2 Images Curtis Jones is poised to leave Liverpool this summer (Image: Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images)

The hip injury that has been cited as the reason behind Curtis Jones' absence from Liverpool's pre-season matches is a 'white lie' designed to disguise the truth, according to reports in the Italian media.

‌



Inter Milan have been keen to sign Jones all summer and it seems they are finally closing in on an agreement. Liverpool rejected a second bid from Inter worth £21.7million way back in June, but the transfer speculation has not subsided.

‌



The Reds have grown frustrated by Inter's approach to negotiations and have reportedly reduced their asking price in an effort to bring things to a conclusion. It means they are ready to shake hands for a lower fee than their original asking price of €40m (£34m).

‌



With all the speculation swirling, Jones has been absent from the last three pre-season matches, against Leeds, Monaco and Como. Asked why, after the 3-2 defeat by Monaco on August 9, manager Andoni Iraola put it down to a minor hip complaint.

‌



“Curtis, he has trained every day but yesterday finished with issues in the hip,” Iraola said. “It doesn’t look anything big but it didn’t make any sense to risk and those are the ones, more or less, closer to a return.”

But having sat out of the 2-0 win over Como on Sunday - which came after Jones returned to training on Wednesday - reports in Italy have shed light on the situation. Sport Mediaset say the medical explanation is a 'white lie'. Instead, he is missing games in an effort to force through the transfer and avoid an injury which could jeopardise things.

Corriere dello Sport report that the Liverpool academy graduate has his heart set on the move to Italy, which will see him link up with John Stones and Djed Spence. Inter have loaned out Davide Frattesi to Lazio, freeing up space, and are ready to make an official bid worth €30m (£25.65m) plus add-ons.

‌



View 2 Images Curtis Jones reportedly wants to move to Inter Milan (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

That is still some way below Liverpool's valuation, but time is running out in the transfer window and Jones has less than a year remaining on his contract. Their bargaining power is limited, with sales needed, having lost Ibrahima Konate, Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah for nothing this summer.

Speaking earlier in the summer, Iraola hinted he wanted to keep Jones, but the situation has changed. “I rate Curtis very highly,” he said. “For me he is a great, great player and I hope he can continue with us and continue performing the way he has been performing.

Article continues below

“It’s very important that he’s scouse, that he’s from here. I also like the personality. From the outside at least he looks like a player with good character and I hope we can keep him, not only for this year but for more time.”

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez gives Andoni Iraola verdict as Arne Slot's issues at Liverpool become clearer
Sports.content:
Milos Kerkez gives Andoni Iraola verdict as Arne Slot's issues at Liverpool become clearer

Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot as Liverpool manager this summer and left-back Milos Kerkez believes the Spaniard's different coaching is already paying off

View 2 Images Milos Kerkez is working with Andoni Iraola once again (Image: Becky Oliver/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Milos Kerkez says he is enjoying the greater freedom he has been given by Andoni Iraola while explaining how the new Liverpool manager's playing style differs from Arne Slot.

‌



Iraola is the man tasked with reviving Liverpool following a bitterly disappointing second campaign under Slot. The Dutchman was dismissed earlier in the summer, with Iraola then hired following three impressive years in charge of Bournemouth.

‌



Liverpool's trademark intensity dropped alarmingly last season, with the high press worryingly erratic at times. Iraola is renowned for his high-energy approach without the ball and his ability to improve young players.

‌



Kerkez spent two seasons under Iraola's management at Bournemouth before making a £40million move to Anfield last summer. He didn't have the desired impact in his debut campaign but is confident that he will flourish, with Iraola's approach better suited to him.

“Everyone hopes so (that Iraola can deliver special times),” Kerkez told the Liverpool Echo when asked how Iraola had changed things. “I mean, it's a big difference, obviously.

‌



“We play really aggressive. We need to run a lot more. It is good. It is tough, but if you want to compete at the top, you need to do that in the Champions League, the Premier League.

“You can see I have more freedom to fly up and down. I'm really running more, with more freedom, putting more balls into boxes. The manager gave me confidence when I was in Bournemouth. We all have to do what he tells us to do. Play aggressive, front-foot, so we need to continue.”

View 2 Images Arne Slot was sacked by Liverpool this summer (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

The Reds begin their 2026/27 campaign away at Newcastle on Sunday after wrapping up pre-season with a 2-0 win over Como. The match was a much-needed morale boost for Liverpool, who had previously suffered high-scoring defeats by Leeds and Monaco.

Both Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong got 90 minutes at full-back, while Jeremy Jacquet scored and impressed alongside Virgil van Dijk in central defence. “He was brilliant, really,” Kerkez said of Jacquet. “Defensively, calm on the ball. Confidence is what we need. Plays hard, plays aggressive. Liverpool style of play, definitely. Really, really good."

New signing Ronald Araujo replaced Jacquet for the second half, helping Alisson keep a timely clean sheet.

“Araujo when he came in second half was aggressive, made a few tackles," Kerkez added. "So was good. JJ good. We were solid. Ali, great, great to keep balls out of the net, so feels good when you have a clean sheet. We have to keep going next week.”

Sports.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi says YES to Man City transfer as £85m deal moves step closer
Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi says YES to Man City transfer as £85m deal moves step closer

Teenage sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi is heading to Manchester City to replace Bernardo Silva and provide new boss Enzo Maresca with a much needed boost

View 2 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi is expected to join Manchester City this week (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/Getty Images)

Manchester City are confident of landing Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi in an £85m deal before the end of this week.

‌



Etihad bosses have advanced talks with their Lille counterparts following the sale of Rodri to Barcelona. The teenage sensation has told his club he wants to leave to join the English giants.

‌



It's understood Bouaddi will agree a five-year-deal with City, that will keep him at the Etihad until 2031 at least. Bouaddi, 18, has emerged as one of the most talented and exciting teenagers in world football.

‌



City chiefs kept close tabs on his progress at this summer's World Cup, once it became clear Rodri would be leaving to return to Spain. Bouaddi impressed at the tournament, starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the last eight.

Enzo Maresca drops new Jack Grealish transfer hint after making Man City return READ MORE :

City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak has been impressed with how Bouaddi has been able to step up on the big occasions as his burgeoning career has developed.

Senior club figures believe Bouaddi's ability to remain unfazed and be able to compete against more senior and experienced players makes him an ideal fit for the City team.

‌



Before the World Cup, Bouaddi had a starring role in Lille's shock Champions League win over Real Madrid in 2024, when he announced himself onto the big stage.

New City boss Enzo Maresca regards Bouaddi as the ideal, long-term replacement for Bernardo Silva, who has joined Real Madrid at the end of last season.

He also broke a record held by Eden Hazard, after making 50 Ligue One appearances for Lille at the age of just 18.

City are still keen to sign a direct replacement for holding midfielder Rodri, but talks with Chelsea about a deal for Enzo Fernandez have stalled.

Sports.content:
Man City accelerate talks for £85m Rodri successor - and could sign Enzo Fernandez as well

Manchester City have wasted no time in moving for new midfielders after agreeing to sell Rodri to Barcelona, with Enzo Maresca keen on Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez

Manchester City are closing in on the signing of Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi as a replacement for Rodri, but haven't ruled out moving for Enzo Fernandez as well.

‌



City have agreed to sell Rodri to Barcelona for around £65million and have moved fast to replace the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner. Barca's interest in the Spain captain has been established for some time, with an opening £38.5m bid rejected earlier this month, so City have been planning ahead.

‌



Bouaddi is one of the most exciting young players in Europe and is valued at £85m by Lille. The 18-year-old midfielder started all five of Morocco's game at this summer's World Cup and already has 88 appearances under his belt for Lille.

‌



City have reached advanced talks with the French side for Bouaddi, according to BBC Sport, who report that manager Enzo Maresca still retains a 'strong interest' in Chelsea's Fernandez. Maresca coached the Argentina international during his spell at Stamford Bridge and wants a reunion at City.

Fernandez joined Chelsea from Benfica in February 2023 for £107m and is valued at over £120m by the Blues now. He was booed by a section of Chelsea fans after coming on as a substitute in their 3-1 pre-season friendly win over Real Sociedad on the weekend and faces an uncertain future.

‌



The 25-year-old had been keen to join Real Madrid in the summer transfer window and was suspended by ex-manager Liam Rosenior for his public flirtation with the Spanish giants. Meanwhile his agent, Javier Pastore, has been agitating for a pay rise for his client.

City missed the chance to trigger the £120m release clause in his contract, with the deadline of 5pm on Friday passing. Despite splashing out £116m for Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest earlier this summer, they are in need of reinforcements in central midfield.

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez's future at Chelsea is uncertain (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

‌



Rodri's departure is a hugely significant one for Maresca, who is also set to lose Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Arabian side Al Qadsiah for a fee of £51m. Anderson started alongside Matteo Kovacic in the Community Shield on Sunday, where Arsenal's 3-0 win underlined the improvement that's needed for City.

Nico Gonzalez and Rico Lewis were used off the bench by Maresca, who is desperate for further reinforcements in the middle of the pitch. The transfer window remains open until September 1, with the money earned from the sales of Rodri and Reijnders able to offset the potential signings of Bouaddi and Fernandez.

Maresca insisted on Sunday that the defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff would not change anything. "We knew already before the game that the things that we need to do, it is not because we lost the game or even if we were winning the game, we [would not think in a] different way," he said post-match.

Article continues below

"We are quite clear about what we need to do. And for sure, as I said, we are going to do something before the window transfer closes."

Sports.title: Liverpool star now banned from playing for them for rest of the year
Sports.content:
Liverpool star now banned from playing for them for rest of the year

A player who impressed for Liverpool in pre-season will not feature under Andoni Iraola this year

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe cannot play for the first-team in 2026 (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe was absent from their final pre-season fixture on Sunday. The Reds rounded off their summer preparation with a double header against Serie A side Como.

‌



Andoni Iraola’s side drew 0-0 in a shortened 70-minute behind-closed-doors friendly at Liverpool’s training centre earlier in the day. They then faced Cesc Fabregas’ men again in a public match, where Cody Gakpo and Jeremy Jacquet’s first-half goals sealed a 2-0 win at Anfield.

‌



However, 18-year-old defender Ndukwe was not involved in either of the games despite Iraola’s two squads consisting of 30 players. That is understood to have been a case of Iraola preferring his other central defensive options over Ndukwe, rather than due to his work permit complications, which will essentially ban him from playing for Liverpool for much of this season.

‌



The centre-back joined from Austria this summer in a £2.6million deal after he turned 18, with the Reds having agreed a deal in principle back in January. Yet, despite impressing for his new club throughout this summer’s pre-season friendlies, he will not be allowed to play when Liverpool make the trip to Newcastle this Sunday for their first Premier League game of the campaign.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jeremy Jacquet scores on Liverpool debut as Cody Gakpo sends reminder - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola singles out three Liverpool stars as boss addresses problem area READ MORE :

Since Brexit, with the UK no longer part of the European Union, clubs now have to navigate a more complex work permit system to ensure players are able to move to England. That is especially the case for those who are yet to establish themselves at the top level.

‌



Liverpool need a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) from the FA to secure a work visa from the Home Office. But the 6ft 6in defender, who came up through Austria Vienna’s academy and made just one senior appearance last season, has not yet accumulated enough points to obtain a GBE to receive a work visa.

Ndukwe cannot play for Liverpool in a competitive game in 2026 because he didn't reach the 15 points target required to qualify for a UK work permit.

Discussions are therefore ongoing over a potential loan move designed to secure his UK work permit. The club are assessing multiple opportunities and a decision is expected over the next two weeks before the summer transfer window shuts.

‌



The better the league Ndukwe plays in, the more points towards a work permit he will earn. It is understood that, with the right move, the necessary points tally could be achieved by January.

View 2 Images The towering defender is expected to be sent out on loan (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

This means Ndukwe may potentially still feature for Liverpool this season, after the turn of the year if he was recalled. But that is a potential drawback for clubs interested in a loan.

‌



Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has already been left impressed by his potential future centre-back partner, labelling Ndukwe a "big talent" after playing alongside him in the first half against Monaco earlier this month.

"Obviously, I saw the games in pre-season in America," Van Dijk said. "Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.

"The matter of fact is that he has to go on loan and wherever he goes, he needs to learn, get better and be ready when he comes back to hopefully stay there."

Article continues below

According to The Mail, clubs in Portugal, Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have all enquired about taking Ndukwe on loan, but there is a sense that Portugal may be his preferred destination.

Sports.title: Colwill hits last-second stunner as Cardiff fight back to deny Wrexham
Sports.content:
Cardiff earned the most dramatic point on their return to the Sky Bet Championship as Rubin Colwill's stunning 98th-minute free-kick earned a 1-1 draw against Wrexham.

Former Bluebirds striker Kieffer Moore had given the visitors the lead with a cracking strike after just two minutes and 26 seconds at the Cardiff City Stadium, in the first meeting between the two Welsh sides in 24 years.

It was his seventh goal against Cardiff - against no side has he scored more in his career.

That looked to be enough to secure a winning start for the Red Dragons, who missed out on a place in the play-offs last season - and thus a chance at a fourth straight promotion - by a margin of just two points.

Cardiff had looked bright in spells, but found clear-cut openings hard to come by - and when Wrexham captain Dom Hyam headed a cross onto his own crossbar, it looked as though their final chance had come and gone.

But after George Dobson brought down Joel Colwill inches outside the penalty area, his older brother fired a beauty into the top-left corner to spark opening-night jubilation in South Wales.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kieffer Moore goal fires Wrexham into the lead inside three minutes against Welsh rivals Cardiff.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stunning Rubin Colwill free-kick snatches 90+8 minute equaliser against Wrexham.

3: GOAL! Danny Imray's ball over the top finds Kieffer Moore all too easily; he waits for it to bounce a couple of times, before catching it perfectly and firing a cracker across Nathan Trott.

6: CHANCE! Wrexham crowd the box, and when a Callum Doyle header is looped in from inside the six-yard box, Nathan Trott has to be alert to tip it over.

22: SAVE! Wrexham debutant Anthony Patterson comes from his line to beat Yousef Salech to a slack pass back to the goalkeeper.

36: OFF THE BAR! Moore rises to meet a corner from the right and sends a header skidding off the top of the bar.

58: OFF THE POST! Wrexham's Callum Doyle opts to go alone instead of finding one of the many team-mates to his right in the box, then crashes a shot off the left-hand upright.

90+5: SO CLOSE! Dom Hyam gets up to defend a looping ball in from the right and crashes a header onto the crossbar and away.

90+6: LATE, LATE DRAMA! George Dobson brings down Joel Colwill inches outside the area and wins a free-kick.

90+8: GOAL! The roof comes off the stadium as Rubin Colwill fires an absolutely beautiful free-kick high into the top-left corner to earn a point for Cardiff.

Barry-Murphy: I had a feeling we may get one more chance

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy speaking on Sky Sports Football:

"It was a difficult night. A very enjoyable night in the end. The game, naturally, didn't go the way we wanted from the start because Wrexham started really well, scored a great goal and that took the wind out of our sails for a while.

"We started to show our quality throughout the course of the game and I just had the feeling at the end we may get one more chance. But, if I'm being honest, I thought it was probably done.

"We had a few games here last year where we found it difficult to break teams down when they were winning and sat deep, so I just tried to find a different solution and tried to get all of our goalscorers on the pitch.

"We got one or two late chances and Rubin provided the defining moment."

Parkinson frustrated Wrexham didn't put game beyond doubt

Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson speaking on Sky Sports Football:

"We've had enough chances to have killed the game off. We felt really comfortable in the game. Of course they're going to come onto us towards the end, but could we have kept the ball better in the corner? We gave a cheap free-kick away and a quality player has stuck it in the top corner.

"In terms of the performance, it was good. I thought there were a lot of good performances out there; we had a real cutting-edge to our attacking play. We should've taken the game out of sight.

"In many respects, I can't ask for much more, but as always, there are areas we can improve on."

Clearlake, under the leadership of Behdad Eghbali and Jose Feliciano, effectively run the club even though Boehly is the chairman.

Daily Mail's Riath Al-Samarrai speaking on Sky Sports News' Paper Talk:

"It's been a very uneasy alliance, almost from the get-go.

Sports.title: Sheff Utd face winding-up hearing as former owner makes claim
Sports.content:
Former Sheff Utd owner United World claims it is still owed £35m from COH Sports Bidco; winding-up hearing set for August 19; if current owners declared insolvent, 12-point deduction could be imposed on Bramall Lane club; sources close to COH insist club is 'financially healthy'

Sheffield United's owners are focused on the new season despite the club's former owners suggesting they face a "real prospect" of administration ahead of an insolvency court hearing on Wednesday.

Sky Sports News reported last month that the club's previous owners, United World, had issued a winding-up petition against the current owners.

United World, which sold Sheffield United to COH Sports Bidco, claims it is still owned £35m for the takeover.

If the £35m owed to United World is paid the threat of administration goes away.

As things stand, though, Sky Sports News understands that a winding-up hearing will take place on August 19 - and sources at United World have told Sky Sports News that it could result in co-owner Steve Rosen being banned from his role.

This is due to EFL Regulation 2.1.16, which states any owner involved in two insolvencies in 10 years can be disqualified.

It is understood that in 2023 US company Invacare suffered an insolvency event and Rosen was non-executive chairman.

It is also understood that if the owners are declared to be insolvent a 12-point deduction could be imposed on the club.

In a statement to Sky Sports News, United World said: "As the former owners of SUFC, United World does not want to see SUFC facing months of uncertainty that will follow the winding-up order being granted on 19 August, but in the absence of [Helmy] Eltoukhy and Rosen, both billionaires, agreeing to pay what they owe, we have no alternative but to take all legal steps to protect our interests.

"We understand that the EFL and the Independent Football Regulator (the IFR) are aware of this situation but so far, we are not aware of any intervention by either.

"United World has issued this public statement in the hope that it is possible to avoid the potential consequences the Club may face if this is not resolved before 19 August, after which we shall have no control over those consequences."

The EFL is aware of the United World statement and will consider any relevant developments in line with its regulations.

Sources close to the Sheffield United ownership said: "We are disappointed Prince Abdullah is trying to hurt the club and its supporters with publicity stunts.

"The deal between sophisticated parties in 2024 was well advised by his financial advisors.

"Sheffield United is financially healthy, unlike under Prince Abdullah when the Club incurred a points deduction for missing payments to football creditors.

"Nonetheless, Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen invited Abdullah to re-invest in the Club and join the ownership of Sheffield United and to help use his skills to support our promotion efforts.

"Helmy and Steve are focused on the sustainability of the club and the season ahead."

Sheffield United started the Championship season with a goalless draw at home to Birmingham.

Sports.title: LIV Golf confirms season-ending event in Michigan cancelled
Sports.content:
LIV Golf has confirmed its season-ending Team Championship event in Michigan will no longer go ahead, with this week's tournament in Indianapolis to be a stroke-play event that concludes the season.

Part of a lengthy LIV Golf statement on Monday read: "With LIV Golf Indianapolis serving as the final event of the season, the previously scheduled Aramco LIV Golf Michigan, originally set for August 27-30, at The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort, will not take place."

As of last Thursday, tickets for LIV Golf's Team Championship event in Michigan could no longer be purchased on its official website amid reports it had been cancelled, while star player Tyrrell Hatton entered a DP World Tour event on the same dates.

The Telegraph reported a day earlier that LIV's players had been told of its cancellation. However nothing was confirmed by the league itself until Monday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryson DeChambeau claims that LIV Golf players were left 'surprised' by the Saudi Public Investment Fund's decision to withdraw funding from the organisation

England's Hatton appeared on the latest version of the entry list for the British Masters, which also runs from August 27-30, live on Sky Sports.

Hatton is joined on the entry list by fellow LIV players Tom McKibbin and Adrian Meronk, with the trio set to tee it up at The Belfry, where the tournament is being hosted by Sir Nick Faldo.

Prior to its cancellation, former Open champion Cameron Smith had said he would be "disappointed" if the Indianapolis event did not go ahead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy reflects on the running of the PGA Tour before LIV came along and shares his concerns over future schedules

LIV's future into 2027 remains in doubt.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced in April it would be ending its financing of the league at the conclusion of the 2026 season, leaving LIV Golf searching for new investors.

League CEO Scott O'Neil announced earlier this month that the league had reached an agreement with a new unnamed 'lead investor' to provide funding for the 2027 season.

O'Neil said the deal was set to be finalised later this month but added the new investor had "signed a term sheet".

Sports.title: Man Utd captain Fernandes not for sale despite Galatasaray interest
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is not for sale at any price despite interest from Galatasaray.

Reports have claimed the Turkish side are ready to bid for the 31-year-old, who has entered the final year of his contract, but United also have an option to extend by a further year.

However, United will not entertain any offers for their talisman, who was named Premier League Player of the Year last season after breaking the competition's assist record.

The £57m release clause for foreign clubs in his contract has now expired.

In December, Fernandes revealed he had been "hurt" when United told him last summer he was free to accept a big-money offer to join Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal, who were ready to pay £100m as a transfer fee.

Despite Fernandes feeling as though the club were open to selling him last summer, the message from the hierarchy since has been clear: he is not for sale.

The ambiguity of last summer has been put to bed with United viewing Fernandes as crucial to the future of their project.

Could Man Utd really sell Fernandes?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch footage of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes returning to training ahead of a new Premier League season! X credit: @ManUtd.

Sky Sports' James Savundra on The Transfer Show:

"It doesn't seem likely in this window but go back 12 months, it felt 50:50. It felt like Manchester United would be willing to sell him if they could recoup £100m to spend on other areas.

"He spoke quite openly about the fact he spoke to the Saudi Pro League and the projects there - before deciding he wanted to commit his future to Manchester United.

"You would think the club would be working on a contract extension because he has one year left - plus that option to extend by a further year, which you'd expect them to do so, otherwise he'd be in a position in January where he could speak to foreign clubs over a free transfer.

"Last season he was just incredible with the assist record - he was the best player in the Premier League last season. He's a massive part of Michael Carrick's plans this season.

"There will come a time when Manchester United think about life after Bruno Fernandes but that won't be this summer. He's so important to their plans in Europe and the Premier League."

Image: Joshua Zirkzee has impressed for Manchester United in pre-season

Sky Sports' News' Danyal Khan:

"The good news for Michael Carrick and United is that two players, in particular, have stood out in pre-season.

"Having perhaps looked a bit tired towards the end of last season, Carrick will be purring to see Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo back to their electric selves in pre-season.

"Mbeumo has looked sharp in front of goal with Amad also appearing full of confidence after an impressive World Cup with Cote d'Ivoire in the summer.

"One player who may have a new chapter at the club is Joshua Zirkzee. Although there is still a possibility his future could be away from Old Trafford, he's looked like a different Zirkzee to the one we've seen in previous seasons.

"Albeit it is pre-season, could Zirkzee provide cover for Fernandes in the No 10 position?

"He was particularly impressive in Dublin against Leeds at a sold-out Croke Park, and in his third season at the club it will be intriguing to see how Carrick uses the Dutchman - if his future is at United."
