World.title: Hockeyroos downed by reigning champions in World Cup pool match
World.content:
The Hockeyroos have been beaten by the Netherlands in their second match of the FIH Hockey World Cup, going down 4-2 despite a battling performance against the reigning champions.

Australia are nevertheless well placed to qualify for the second round with the group's other result going their way.

Rejuvenated Hockeyroos and Kookaburras tackle World Cup with fresh perspectives The Kookaburras and Hockeyroos' last major tournament was Paris 2024 where they exited in the quarter-finals. They have both experienced significant change since then, and are determined to start their new eras with success at the World Cup.

The Aussies took Monday's game to their hosts from the opening whistle in the Amsterdam suburb of Amstelveen, producing a strong first quarter and putting the world number one team under sustained pressure.

The Hockeyroos earned a startling eight penalty corners in the opening term, including seven in succession, but were unable to find the breakthrough.

Australia paid for their profligacy as the Dutch showed them how it is done, scoring with their first penalty corner through Yibbi Jansen in the 13th minute.

The Netherlands doubled their advantage in contentious circumstances.

Australia referred Joosje Burg's goal for a potential back stick in the build-up, with replays showing the ball had made contact with the back of a Dutch stick. However, because the incident occurred outside the attacking 23-metre area, it was deemed non-referable, and the goal stood.

Refusing to let the setback halt their momentum, the Hockeyroos continued to attack and were eventually rewarded through Steph Kershaw, who found the back of the net in the 23rd minute to reduce the deficit.

Kershaw was involved again as Australia drew level at 2-2, getting the faintest of touches on an Abi Williams flick to set up a thrilling finish against the tournament favourites.

With the match in the balance heading into the final quarter, the Netherlands showed why they are the world's top-ranked side.

The Dutch piled pressure on the Australian defence, earning five penalty corners in the final quarter, scoring twice in the space of four minutes through Burg and Marjin Veen to take control of Group A.

The Hockeyroos now turn their attention to Chile on Wednesday from 5:30pm, AEST.

Chile are pointless having lost 3-0 to Japan.

With Australia beating Japan 2-0 in their opening game, a Hockeyroos victory will ensure their progress to the next stage, unless Japan unexpectedly beat the Dutch. In that case, goal difference will come into play so Australia will be seeking a large win over the South Americans.

AAP

World.title: Swans coach 'disappointed' over Melbourne incident
World.content:
Sydney Swans coach Dean Cox says he is "disappointed" regarding allegations of sexual assault involving several players in Melbourne on Sunday night and that the club will have more to say on the issue today.

The incident has delayed the announcement of the AFL's All Australian squad, which was to have been named today but has now been pushed back to Monday.

Police are continuing to investigate the alleged assault at the Pullman Hotel near the MCG, where the Swans were staying following their 36-point win over Essendon.

Victoria Police issued a statement on Monday saying detectives were investigating a report of a sexual assault in East Melbourne.

"The incident occurred at a hotel on Wellington Parade in the early hours of the morning," a spokesperson said.

"The exact circumstances are yet to be established, and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing."

Police were investigating the alleged sexual assault at the Pullman Hotel in east Melbourne. (ABC News)

On Tuesday morning, Cox spoke briefly to the media outside the Swans' headquarters in Sydney.

"Obviously extremely disappointed with what's happened and we understand there are questions and we'll update as we gather more information," he said.

Cox said it was too early to say whether the players involved would face sanctions from the AFL.

"We're working our way through everything with the AFL and the relevant parties and we'll update when we get more information," he said.

He said he had not yet spoken to the players but would do so "as the day unfolds".

At least one Swans player was expected to have been named in the All Australian squad which was due to be named today but has now been delayed.

Players named in the team were due to appear onstage at the AFL Awards Night on Tuesday next week.

Matthew Pavlich says the club is looking into what happened in Melbourne.

Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich said on Monday that the club was still piecing together what happened in Melbourne and was undertaking its own internal inquiries.

"Safe to say, we're extremely shocked and disappointed that this has taken place and that the players have found themselves in this situation," he said.

"We understand the level of interest in the matter, and there's going to be lots of speculation, but given it's a police matter right now, that's all that we can say."

The AFL is yet to comment beyond the brief statement the organisation released yesterday.

"The club made the AFL aware of the matter which is currently under Victoria Police investigation," the statement read.

World.title: Fungi fans celebrate its recognition as nature's third living kingdom
World.content:
Mycelium would not know or care if it was recognised by the Australian Labor Party.

Its priority over millions of years has been to work underground in ways that scientists are only beginning to appreciate.

But the ALP has a soft spot for mycelium, and all other forms of fungi.

At its recent national conference, federal Environment Minister Murray Watt explicitly recognised fungi as part of Australia's natural environment and biodiversity, separate and equal to flora and fauna.

"Fungi are vital to our ecosystem, and it is crucial that our environmental and biodiversity frameworks reflect this," Senator Watt told the conference.

Australia has as many as 250,000 fungal species. (Supplied: Stephen Axford)

The recognition follows years of advocacy by mycologists, biologists, ecologists and Australian citizen-scientist organisation Fungimap.

They are part of a global network of fungi fans celebrating the recent addition of the word "funga" to the Cambridge Dictionary to describe the third kingdom of living things.

FUNGA noun [u] biology, environment specialized All the fungi (=organisms that usually grow on and get their food from decaying material or other living things) that grow in a particular area or a particular period in time ~ Cambridge Dictionary

Fungimap committee member Catherine Marciniak, a grassroots ALP member of the Ballina branch in northern New South Wales, was one of the driving forces behind the party's recognition of fungi in its national platform.

Delicate species of fungi grow side-by-side. (Supplied: Catherine Marciniak)

The revised national platform commits Labor to conserving and restoring "flora, fauna, fungi, oceans and waterways", and could potentially lead to an amendment to the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act.

Ms Marciniak said recognition meant fungi would be included in biodiversity assessments, environmental planning, threatened species monitoring and research opportunities.

"Our concern was, if it's invisible, then it's not measured, and if it's not measured, it's not conserved," she said.

"For instance, we have a critically endangered rainforest right on our doorstep here … [that] has been surveyed for plants and animals, it's been surveyed for butterflies, but it's never been surveyed for a whole kingdom of life.

" We have no endangered species listed for fungi, which is madness. "

Stephen Axford and Catherine Marciniak are behind the push for fungi recognition. (Supplied: Planet Fungi)

Michael Priest, a former mycologist with the NSW Department of Primary Industries and Fungimap president, said fungi played a vital role in recycling nutrients, building healthy soils, carbon storage and supporting the health of up to 95 per cent of the Earth's trees.

Michael Priest says fungi form at least a third of all living things. (Supplied: Michael Priest)

"They underpin everything that we know of what's going on in our ecosystem," he said.

Dr Priest said with about 250,000 species of fungi in Australia and only about 12,000 formally described, there was still much to learn, including potential industrial and medical uses.

He said recognising them as a separate type of organism would put Australia in step with many other countries, including Chile and the United Kingdom.

"There are more fungi than there are plants, and if you were to take the insects out of the animal kingdom, there'd be more fungi than there are animals," Dr Priest said.

"We think that they play an equal role to plants and animals, and so they should be recognised equally."

World.title: ‘Be quiet’: Trump berates reporter who asked about his relationship with female staffer
World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaUS politics ‘Be quiet’: Trump berates reporter who asked about his relationship with female staffer Michael Koziol August 18, 2026 — 8:35am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Washington: Donald Trump and his White House aides savaged a reporter who asked about his relationship with a female staffer, bringing to the fore an innuendo that has circulated in Washington for some time. CNN journalist Kristen Holmes asked the US president about his aide Natalie Harp after a Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff, told a rally that Trump “wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenceless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar”. Loading It was a rare occasion on which a well-known Democratic politician publicly raised the issue of Harp, a White House staffer and member of Trump’s inner circle who frequently prints out articles from conservative news platforms for him to read, or types out his Truth Social posts. She was also one of a handful of close aides to secretly travel with Trump on an alternative flight from Turkey last month, rather than take his Air Force One jet, which was deemed a security risk amid threats from Iran.



Harp’s close relationship with Trump has been scrutinised in the press. The New York Times reported in 2024 that Harp wrote him fawning letters, leaving them in his personal spaces, including one that said: “You are all that matters to me.” On Monday (Washington time), Holmes asked Trump for his response to Ossoff’s public remarks. He initially took aim at Ossoff. Natalie Harp disembarking Air Force One on the weekend. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson “You mean Pee-wee Herman? Pee-wee Herman lookalike,” he said, referring to the childish American comedic character portrayed by Paul Reubens. “No, I would much rather do other things.” He then spoke at length about the White House ballroom. But later, after Holmes attempted to ask another question about an unrelated matter, Trump turned on her, repeatedly telling her to stop talking.



“You’re very disrespectful … You’re fake news,” he said. “You’re a loud, boisterous person. You’re fake news. Be quiet, be quiet, be quiet. You’re a fake reporter, and you report fake news.” Those remarks were then boosted online by an official White House social media channel, Rapid Response 47, which called Holmes a “scumbag” and explicitly linked Trump’s outburst to her question about Harp. Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff raised Harp’s name at a rally. AP “[Holmes] is a disgraceful, humiliating embarrassment to her alleged profession,” the account said. “[Trump] hosts a hero lifeguard in the Oval Office and she uses it as an opportunity to take a cheap shot about one of President Trump’s staffers. These scumbags are the lowest of the low.” The official White House account, which has 2.2 million followers, also attacked Holmes as a mother. “Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question,” it said. “They will be sickened and embarrassed to have a parent be so callous and vindictive. It’s quite troubling.”



In a statement, CNN defended its reporter and said she had asked a tough, relevant and newsworthy question. “Public officials are free to challenge reporting they disagree with, but personal attacks on journalists for asking questions are beneath the office and inconsistent with the principles of a free press,” the network said. “We stand firmly behind Kristen and reject these attacks in the strongest possible terms.” Trump Harp step off from Marine One on Sunday. AP Photo/Jose Luis Magana Trump regularly attacks CNN and its reporters, especially women, including anchor Kaitlan Collins. During a poorly received speech at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner last month, he complained that Collins habitually failed to smile despite being “a young, attractive woman”. Harp, 34, is officially an executive assistant to the president. She spoke at the 2020 Republican National Convention, where she credited Trump with saving her life by legalising right-to-try therapies – although subsequent reporting cast doubt on those claims. She later worked for right-wing site One America News.



In their recent book Regime Change, journalists Jonathan Swan and Maggie Haberman reported that Trump called Harp “Nathalie”, using a French pronunciation, and told staff she was the only aide who loved him as much as his own wife and children. “All of you will go off and make money,” he would say, according to Regime Change. “She’ll never leave me.” Harp pictured last year with White House communications director Steven Cheung. World.title: Alleged pork plotters linked to $10 million smuggling scheme
World.content:
NationalQueenslandCCC Alleged pork plotters linked to $10 million smuggling scheme Courtney Kruk August 18, 2026 — 8:28am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Four people have been charged with financial crimes including fraud after meat freight trucks were allegedly used to transport millions of dollars between Queensland and NSW over a nine-year period. Police say the accused were all business owners or representatives within the pork industry, and allege they deleted or purposely did not create records for sales amounting to about $10 million between 2017 and 2026. It is alleged the money was retained for personal use and not included in business records. A joint investigation led by Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission has uncovered a large-scale interstate fraud operation with connections to the pork meat industry. Carl Court/Getty Images Investigators further allege that during the nearly 10-year period, more than $30 million was transported from NSW to Queensland, with substantial amounts of cash concealed in freight vehicles.



Two individuals from Queensland are also accused of incorrectly relabelling frozen meat products to reflect new production and best-before dates. According to investigators, this has not raised food safety concerns. The investigation – dubbed “Operation Ragamuffin” – was led by Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission and the New South Wales Police Force’s Anti-Money Laundering Unit. More than $3 million in cash and two vehicles were seized during the operation. Police say the total value of assets currently held as suspected proceeds of crime exceeded $25 million. The CCC has charged two people from Queensland with fraudulently destroying records, making fraudulent omissions, fraud, receiving tainted property and making false declarations. They are due to appear in Brisbane Magistrates Court in September.



Related Article Queensland Police Scathing police finance report puts former leadership in CCC sights NSW police have charged two people from that state with destroying or concealing accounting records with intent to defraud. One person will face additional charges relating to the possession and dissemination of child abuse material, and the possession of animal abuse material. CCC acting senior executive officer (crime) Cameron Rentz said the commission was committed to disrupting serious criminal offending that undermined the integrity of legitimate business activity. “Complex financial crime is often sophisticated and deliberately concealed.



“The outcome of this investigation demonstrates the value of intelligence-led operations and strong co-operation between law-enforcement agencies.” NSWPF anti-money laundering unit co-ordinator Detective Inspector Gilbert Laverdure said cross-border criminal networks should expect to be identified and investigated. “The NSWPF will continue to work closely with partner agencies to detect, disrupt and prosecute any serious offending,” he said. World.title: The Test team’s five biggest problems: Is Lyon an automatic selection?
World.content:
Analysis SportCricketAustralian cricket The Test team’s five biggest problems: Is Lyon an automatic selection? Daniel Brettig Updated August 18, 2026 — 7:51am ,first published 5:52pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Top order batting – Pat Cummins asked his batting order to get through a tricky first couple of hours on a fresh pitch in Darwin and they were completely unable to find a way to do so against a diligent but far from fearsome Bangladesh attack. Jake Weatherald’s perpetual motion at the crease speaks of technical tweaks but also nerves, and it is tough to see him keeping his place in Mackay. Marnus Labuschagne has already been dropped and recalled once in the past year, but is still struggling to find his best. Then there’s Travis Head and the question of his best position. Former opener Matthew Hayden was one seasoned voice to call for Matt Renshaw and Sam Konstas at the top, with Head moving to three. Ebadot Hossain of Bangladesh celebrates after taking the wicket of Marnus Labuschagne. Getty Images Tellingly, Cummins spoke not of a one-off problem but of a trend, meaning that the team’s batting difficulties will be the chief topic of internal conversation this week. He was also open about the selectors’ ability to make change: “Every Aussie Test we do you can kind of pick whatever, it’s not a World Cup squad. You’ve got a lot of available guys who are ready to go.” As Alyssa Healy put it on Fox Cricket: “It’s almost like they’ve underestimated themselves a little bit, the Bangladeshis. I mean, the whole of Australia probably did as well, but it’s almost like their humble approach has worked for them. We’ve got carried away with how big this summer is, but this is a wake-up call for Australia. Probably what they needed as well, after breezing through last summer.”



Nathan Lyon – In his first game back from hamstring surgery, 38-year-old Lyon was ineffective, certainly relative to the Bangladesh spinners, and also dropped a vital catch. There is no doubt Australia will need Lyon’s skills in India next year, but questions must be asked about whether he is an automatic selection, either ahead of Scott Boland or also the younger left-arm spinner Matt Kuhnemann. Meanwhile, Lyon needs to regain his ability to deceive batsmen in the air – Bangladesh had few problems reading his length here, despite a helpful breeze at times. Editor's pick Updated

Australian cricket Cummins flags batting changes after Australia’s bubble burst by Bangladesh Cummins said of Boland: “With Scotty, we all know how good he is, so we’ll turn up in Mackay, have a look at the pitch and work out your best bowling group. But with someone like Scotty in the squad you’re always trying to find a way to fit him in, he’s that good.” Domestic pitches – Something an excellent Darwin surface exposed was how Bangladesh’s batters were better equipped to keep out good balls and bat time, a theme that runs well down the ranks into the Sheffield Shield. Partly this is because of a preponderance of grassy result pitches that make life difficult for batters and a little too easy for seamers.



A topic of conversation at a recent Cricket Australia summit in Brisbane, it’s an issue that Head has highlighted the difficulty of: “You can sit outside and say we want a great balance between bat and ball, but if you ask the states and the boards and who runs the show, they’ll say we want to win Shields, so I don’t think they’d care less on what it looks like, they want performance and they want to win.” Talent pipeline – A major reason Australia are fielding their oldest ever Test team is a high level of selection scepticism about the younger talent coming through, something backed up by modest Shield aggregates in recent summers. Australian coach Andrew McDonald and Josh Hazlewood. Getty Images Based on those figures, there is no-one better available, but it will be up to the selectors to make some calculated gambles that go beyond pure statistics. Bangladesh provided a good reminder of that by how 25-year-old Tanzid Hasan (first-class batting average 39) and 26-year-old Hasan Mahmud (bowling average 28) seized their opportunities. Succession plan – Australia’s huge allotment of Tests over the next 12 months leaves open the question of whether the current regime will change out of exhaustion as much as anything else next year. But the conversations need to start now, and in some cases they already have.



Head coach Andrew McDonald’s deal expires at the end of 2027, while Cummins’ captaincy tenure is also of uncertain duration. It may be easier to replace McDonald with one of Ryan Harris, Adam Voges or Tim Paine, but it is also a concern that Cummins’ stand-in remains the 37-year-old Steve Smith, whose career has operated on a series by series basis for several years. No foul play is suspected in the death of American actor Hayden Panettiere, police said, as emergency dispatch audio published by several US outlets indicated the star was in cardiac arrest following a suspected overdose. The 36-year-old died at her South Carolina home on Monday (AEST). Hayden Panettiere in 2023. Her father announced her death on Monday. Getty Images Best known for her roles in TV shows Heroes and Nashville, her death was confirmed by her father Skip Panettiere in a statement to US media. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” he said. “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her – and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”



Related Article Updated

Vale Nashville star Hayden Panettiere dies at age 36 Early on Tuesday morning (AEST), Greenville Police said in a statement that emergency services were called to Panettiere’s home at 1.51pm on Sunday after she was found to be unresponsive by a friend. It remains unclear who made the 911 call. Medical assistance was given, but she was pronounced dead at the scene. “The preliminary investigation has not indicated any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances,” police said in the statement. The case is under investigation by the police department and the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.



“An autopsy was completed today. At autopsy, no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to the death,” the statement said. The Greenville County Coroner’s Office also confirmed Panettiere’s death, noting in a statement that she was “found unresponsive inside the residence where she had been temporarily staying”. Panettiere rose to fame in the TV series Heroes, before landing roles in Nashville, Scream 4 and the Bring It On series. Getty Responders reportedly “initiated advanced cardiac life support measures”, which can include breathing tubes, defibrillators and emergency intravenous medications. However, these efforts were unsuccessful, and Panettiere was pronounced dead at 2.32pm (local time). The official cause and manner of the actor’s death remain unknown, and would be determined following further investigation and “the completion of additional studies”, the coroner’s office said.



Related Video Video icon 2:07 Actress Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36 US outlet People reported that emergency workers were heard discussing an “overdose” and “cardiac arrest” in dispatch audio obtained by the publication and other outlets including TMZ. According to several US reports, the actor flew out of Los Angeles with her on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson the day before she died. It remains unclear whether Hickerson was the friend who found her unresponsive on Monday (AEST). Panettiere died a few days before her 37th birthday, which would have been on Friday. She began her acting career at the age of four, with a role in the soap opera One Life to Live as Sarah Roberts. She was perhaps best recognised as Claire Bennet in the popular sci-fi series Heroes, and as Juliette Barnes in Nashville. She also had various film roles including in Remember the Titans and Scream 4. This year, she released a memoir titled This Is Me: A Reckoning. In it, she recounted the impact of being a child actor, her past alcohol addiction and giving up custody of her daughter in 2018.



Panettiere entered an in-patient treatment centre in early 2020 where she worked on overcoming her opioid and alcohol addiction. Though she remained largely out of the spotlight for a few years, Panettiere re-emerged in May to promote her memoir. World.title: ‘The money will come’: Why Pritchard brothers turned down PNG riches to stay in rugby
World.content:
Exclusive SportRugby UnionWallabies ‘The money will come’: Why Pritchard brothers turned down PNG riches to stay in rugby Jonathan Drennan August 18, 2026 — 7:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Before making the biggest decision of their young professional careers, Treyvon and Kadin Pritchard thought back to two important lessons taught to them by their parents, Daniel and Brenda: never leave a job half done, and always show loyalty to those who backed you from the start. The brothers ultimately turned down the lucrative offer tabled by the PNG Chiefs to join the NRL expansion franchise for its inaugural season in 2028, opting instead to remain at their respective rugby clubs, with Treyvon signing an extension with the Reds until 2029 and Kadin remaining at the Brumbies until 2030. Both brothers also have the opportunity to play sevens in the 2028 Olympics. Treyvon (L) and Kadin Pritchard are staying in Australian rugby. Rugby Australia “I think from a young age mum and dad have always instilled in us the value of finishing what you’ve started and never doing a half job,” Treyvon told this masthead. “Our parents taught us to finish what we’ve started. Loyalty does come into play, too. It’s a big part of our everyday lives and something that our parents have made us follow, and it’s led into our everyday life.



“Also, coming through from being a 15-year-old in the Reds environment to moving up and training with the older boys while I was still in school with a couple of my mates. “We all have come through at the same time and we have those connections, and I think a big thing with footy is being able to trust your teammates. If you already have something in place, there’s no real reason to kind of change that and switch it up. Treyvon is one of the most exciting talents in Australian rugby. World Rugby “So I think the friendships and the connections that I already have are also a big part of my reasoning to stay in Australian rugby.” The brothers spoke highly of their dealings with the Chiefs, but ultimately turned down the lucrative offer because they felt they have unfinished business in rugby together – and believe the money will follow them eventually.



“Obviously, it was exciting [to get the PNG offer] and yeah, we did meet with them, and I think that was probably both our first real kind interest from league. So we tested the waters and we were trying to see what it was all about,” Treyvon said. “But I think Rugby Australia had a lot to offer as well. Like I said before, loyalty played a big part in where we are now and that helped us to a decision on where we wanted to be for the next couple of years... “The money is going to come, it’s probably not the biggest worry at the moment. We need to focus on establishing ourselves in our respective teams.” Kadin said that beyond immediate financial rewards, rugby will offer the brothers a chance to travel the world while playing the game they love. “I love rugby union and the possibilities that it can bring with the worldwide game were a big thing for me to stay here,” Kadin said.



“To travel around the world, playing international teams – and even if it’s club level, you can go over somewhere like France. The possibilities of doing that sort of thing, you don’t get that in other sports.” The Ella brothers brought an almost telepathic understanding to the Wallabies back line in the 1980s and the Pritchards believe they can eventually replicate that synergy as a centre partnership for the Australian Test team. Kadin Pritchard dreams of forming a centre partnership with Treyvon at Test level for the Wallabies . Getty Images “It’s definitely a dream of ours to link up at some point,” Kadin said. “We’ve been separated for a reason: to build ourselves up in our own teams and build the groups around us. “By the time we get to the Wallabies, we’ll be set to go, because we’ve got that brother intuition ... we want to play together in the centres, with Trayvon at inside centre.



“It’s definitely been a thought in my mind becoming that 12 and 13, and you probably don’t see it too often having brothers in the centres with that connection. We’re just almost interlinked and we know how each other plays from doing it so often in the backyard.” Having spent endless hours playing together as kids, the two brothers came up against each other for the first time last season, when the Reds faced the Brumbies in Super Rugby. But Treyvon says it is when playing together on the same side that their close relationship brings an extra edge. “We probably don’t have to speak as much as other players would; we can communicate with our body language and trust is a big factor in the connection that we have over other players,” Treyvon said. At 22 years old, Kadin has always felt protective of Treyvon, who is three years younger than him. Treyvon affectionately calls Kadin the family’s “test dummy”, the older brother who had to forge the way into professional rugby before passing on the lessons learned along the way. Though separated by distance, the brothers still speak regularly and operate as a unit when it comes to making decisions on their rugby future.



The brothers have been brought up to support one another, wary that there will always be others outside the family who want to tear one or another of them down. “We know what each other can do and why should we hate on our family when you’ve got haters outside already,” Kadin said. “The tightness of our family, it’s just been brought through by our dad. Treyvon Pritchard suffered serious injuries in this hip drop tackle against Wales at the Junior World Championship, but is recovering well after surgery. Stan Sport “We’re our own biggest supporters, we’ve got to support each other and build each other up so there’s no hate coming from within, and we have a support group here. “There’s no way I’m going to hate on what my bro’s doing. I’m just going to hype him up to be the best player in the world. What’s the point of trying to pull him down when everybody else is trying to do that?”



Both brothers are currently recovering from injuries. Kadin is nursing a hamstring strain but hopes to return to play for the Brumbies in the Super Rugby AUS competition, while Treyvon is recovering from an operation after breaking his right leg ain a hip drop tackle while representing Australia Under 20s. Treyvon’s current recovery timeline is between 12 and 18 weeks. Related Article Australian rugby ‘Run us off our feet’: Wallabies’ surprising ploy to prepare for Japanese heat Both brothers are focused on establishing their positions with their respective Super Rugby clubs ahead of a new season, but Treyvon is aware there will always be future possibilities, whether in rugby or the NRL. “We’re definitely not closed off to playing overseas, and I think once we make a decision on that, I think we would probably look to play together, I don’t see why we wouldn’t,” Treyvon said. “I think living in a different country is hard enough, so I think being with the older bro would be awesome. “I’m [also] not closed off to the NRL. Obviously all the noise that’s been happening recently probably sparked a bit of interest for everyone, but it’s definitely an option down the track. I’m with the Reds for three years and with Aussie rugby for three years, so whatever happens after that happen.” News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

World.title: ASX set to slide, Wall Street retreats as oil prices climb; BHP, CSL results ahead
World.content:
Updated BusinessMarketsWorld markets ASX set to slide, Wall Street retreats as oil prices climb; BHP, CSL results ahead Stan Choe Updated August 18, 2026 — 6:24am ,first published 5:22am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

US stocks edged further from their record heights on Monday after rising oil prices cranked up the pressure on inflation and financial markets. The S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent but remains near its all-time high set Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 272 points, or 0.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.3 per cent. Wall Street opened the week with more losses. Bloomberg The Australian sharemarket is set to decline, with futures at 6.04am AEST pointing to a fall of 40 points, or 0.5 per cent, at the open. The ASX lost 0.5 per cent on Monday. The Australian dollar is stronger at US71.03¢. Reporting season continues with BHP and CSL results slated to be released today. Wall Street’s losses solidified in the afternoon when oil prices accelerated upward. The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, rose 2.7 per cent to $US90.87.



Related Article Exclusive

James Packer James Packer’s bets on AI pay off after sell-down in gaming shares It’s been careening back and forth because of uncertainty about what the war with Iran will do to the global flow of crude. Last month alone, Brent zigzagged between $US72 and $US102 as hopes rose and fell that the United States and Iran could reach a deal that would allow oil tankers to freely exit the Persian Gulf again. Monday’s rally for oil prices sent Treasury yields in the bond market higher, which in turn raised the pressure on the economy and prices for all kinds of investments. The yield on the 10-year Treasury climbed to 4.72 per cent from 4.68 per cent late Friday. It has shot up from just 3.97 per cent before the war with Iran, largely because higher oil prices are worsening inflation and upping the probability that the Federal Reserve will have to hike interest rates. Higher rates could keep a lid on inflation, but they do so by intentionally slowing the economy. The average long-term US mortgage rate has already jumped near its highest level in a year because of the rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, though reports last week said that inflation in July was not as bad as earlier in the summer.



Usually around this time of year, anticipation is building on Wall Street to hear from the head of the Federal Reserve about where it may take interest rates. But the Fed’s new chairman, Kevin Warsh, may give little insight at this year’s economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, at the end of this month, according to Thierry Wizman, a strategist at Macquarie Group Warsh has been adamant about giving Wall Street less guidance about the Fed’s plans for interest rates. Wall Street has run to records despite high inflation in large part because profits are booming for U.S. companies. Those in the S&P 500 index are on track to deliver growth of roughly 50 per cent for earnings per share in the spring from a year earlier, according to FactSet. That’s much better than analysts expected and would be the best since five years ago, when the economy was erupting out of the chasm created by the COVID pandemic. Nearly all the companies in the S&P 500 have turned in their profit reports for the spring. Still to come are big retailers, including reports this week from Home Depot, Target and Walmart.



Related Article Opinion

Trump's America Trump makes America Inc’s grip on the world even tighter They’re facing pressure. Their customers’ incomes may be turning iffier after U.S. employers surprisingly cut more jobs last month than they added. At the same time, their customers are continuing to see bills rise quickly as inflation remains much higher than anyone would like. A report last week said that shoppers surprisingly spent less at U.S. retailers last month than in June, and CEOs for retailers could give color this week on what they’re seeing. On Wall Street, trading was relatively quiet Monday. L3Harris Technologies fell 4.6 per cent after the defense company said Christopher Kubasik stepped down as its CEO and chairman following “certain conduct by Kubasik that was not consistent with the values of the Company.” It gave few details but said the conduct was not related to its financial reporting, controls, customer relationships or operational performance.



Alphabet dipped 0.5 per cent even though Berkshire Hathaway said it increased its investment in Google’s parent company, along with several homebuilders. Berkshire built a reputation for buying stocks at affordable prices under its former CEO, famed investor Warren Buffett. Constellation Brands fell 6.2 per cent after Berkshire said it sold all its holdings in the seller of Modelo beer and Robert Mondavi wine. All told, the S&P 500 fell 40.70 points to 7,745.06. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 272.63 to 53,459.78, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 84.25 to 26,644.91. In stock markets abroad, indexes dipped in Europe following a stronger finish in Asia. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.7 per cent after a report said Japan’s economy grew at a slower pace in the April-June quarter than economists expected. Indexes jumped 1.3 per cent in Hong Kong and 1.4 per cent in Shanghai for some of the world’s biggest moves.

World.title: ‘Be quiet’: Trump berates reporter who asked about his relationship with female staffer
World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaUS politics ‘Be quiet’: Trump berates reporter who asked about his relationship with female staffer Michael Koziol August 18, 2026 — 8:35am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Washington: Donald Trump and his White House aides savaged a reporter who asked about his relationship with a female staffer, bringing to the fore an innuendo that has circulated in Washington for some time. CNN journalist Kristen Holmes asked the US president about his aide Natalie Harp after a Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff, told a rally that Trump “wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenceless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar”. Loading It was a rare occasion on which a well-known Democratic politician publicly raised the issue of Harp, a White House staffer and member of Trump’s inner circle who frequently prints out articles from conservative news platforms for him to read, or types out his Truth Social posts. She was also one of a handful of close aides to secretly travel with Trump on an alternative flight from Turkey last month, rather than take his Air Force One jet, which was deemed a security risk amid threats from Iran.



Harp’s close relationship with Trump has been scrutinised in the press. The New York Times reported in 2024 that Harp wrote him fawning letters, leaving them in his personal spaces, including one that said: “You are all that matters to me.” On Monday (Washington time), Holmes asked Trump for his response to Ossoff’s public remarks. He initially took aim at Ossoff. Natalie Harp disembarking Air Force One on the weekend. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson “You mean Pee-wee Herman? Pee-wee Herman lookalike,” he said, referring to the childish American comedic character portrayed by Paul Reubens. “No, I would much rather do other things.” He then spoke at length about the White House ballroom. But later, after Holmes attempted to ask another question about an unrelated matter, Trump turned on her, repeatedly telling her to stop talking.



“You’re very disrespectful … You’re fake news,” he said. “You’re a loud, boisterous person. You’re fake news. Be quiet, be quiet, be quiet. You’re a fake reporter, and you report fake news.” Those remarks were then boosted online by an official White House social media channel, Rapid Response 47, which called Holmes a “scumbag” and explicitly linked Trump’s outburst to her question about Harp. Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff raised Harp’s name at a rally. AP “[Holmes] is a disgraceful, humiliating embarrassment to her alleged profession,” the account said. “[Trump] hosts a hero lifeguard in the Oval Office and she uses it as an opportunity to take a cheap shot about one of President Trump’s staffers. These scumbags are the lowest of the low.” The official White House account, which has 2.2 million followers, also attacked Holmes as a mother. “Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question,” it said. “They will be sickened and embarrassed to have a parent be so callous and vindictive. It’s quite troubling.”



In a statement, CNN defended its reporter and said she had asked a tough, relevant and newsworthy question. “Public officials are free to challenge reporting they disagree with, but personal attacks on journalists for asking questions are beneath the office and inconsistent with the principles of a free press,” the network said. “We stand firmly behind Kristen and reject these attacks in the strongest possible terms.” Trump Harp step off from Marine One on Sunday. AP Photo/Jose Luis Magana Trump regularly attacks CNN and its reporters, especially women, including anchor Kaitlan Collins. During a poorly received speech at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner last month, he complained that Collins habitually failed to smile despite being “a young, attractive woman”. Harp, 34, is officially an executive assistant to the president. She spoke at the 2020 Republican National Convention, where she credited Trump with saving her life by legalising right-to-try therapies – although subsequent reporting cast doubt on those claims. She later worked for right-wing site One America News.



In their recent book Regime Change, journalists Jonathan Swan and Maggie Haberman reported that Trump called Harp “Nathalie”, using a French pronunciation, and told staff she was the only aide who loved him as much as his own wife and children. “All of you will go off and make money,” he would say, according to Regime Change. “She’ll never leave me.” Harp pictured last year with White House communications director Steven Cheung. World.title: Alleged pork plotters linked to $10 million smuggling scheme
World.content:
NationalQueenslandCCC Alleged pork plotters linked to $10 million smuggling scheme Courtney Kruk August 18, 2026 — 8:28am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Four people have been charged with financial crimes including fraud after meat freight trucks were allegedly used to transport millions of dollars between Queensland and NSW over a nine-year period. Police say the accused were all business owners or representatives within the pork industry, and allege they deleted or purposely did not create records for sales amounting to about $10 million between 2017 and 2026. It is alleged the money was retained for personal use and not included in business records. A joint investigation led by Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission has uncovered a large-scale interstate fraud operation with connections to the pork meat industry. Carl Court/Getty Images Investigators further allege that during the nearly 10-year period, more than $30 million was transported from NSW to Queensland, with substantial amounts of cash concealed in freight vehicles.



Two individuals from Queensland are also accused of incorrectly relabelling frozen meat products to reflect new production and best-before dates. According to investigators, this has not raised food safety concerns. The investigation – dubbed “Operation Ragamuffin” – was led by Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission and the New South Wales Police Force’s Anti-Money Laundering Unit. More than $3 million in cash and two vehicles were seized during the operation. Police say the total value of assets currently held as suspected proceeds of crime exceeded $25 million. The CCC has charged two people from Queensland with fraudulently destroying records, making fraudulent omissions, fraud, receiving tainted property and making false declarations. They are due to appear in Brisbane Magistrates Court in September.



Related Article Queensland Police Scathing police finance report puts former leadership in CCC sights NSW police have charged two people from that state with destroying or concealing accounting records with intent to defraud. One person will face additional charges relating to the possession and dissemination of child abuse material, and the possession of animal abuse material. CCC acting senior executive officer (crime) Cameron Rentz said the commission was committed to disrupting serious criminal offending that undermined the integrity of legitimate business activity. “Complex financial crime is often sophisticated and deliberately concealed.



“The outcome of this investigation demonstrates the value of intelligence-led operations and strong co-operation between law-enforcement agencies.” NSWPF anti-money laundering unit co-ordinator Detective Inspector Gilbert Laverdure said cross-border criminal networks should expect to be identified and investigated. “The NSWPF will continue to work closely with partner agencies to detect, disrupt and prosecute any serious offending,” he said. Getty Images Based on those figures, there is no-one better available, but it will be up to the selectors to make some calculated gambles that go beyond pure statistics. Bangladesh provided a good reminder of that by how 25-year-old Tanzid Hasan (first-class batting average 39) and 26-year-old Hasan Mahmud (bowling average 28) seized their opportunities. Succession plan – Australia’s huge allotment of Tests over the next 12 months leaves open the question of whether the current regime will change out of exhaustion as much as anything else next year. But the conversations need to start now, and in some cases they already have.



Head coach Andrew McDonald’s deal expires at the end of 2027, while Cummins’ captaincy tenure is also of uncertain duration. It may be easier to replace McDonald with one of Ryan Harris, Adam Voges or Tim Paine, but it is also a concern that Cummins’ stand-in remains the 37-year-old Steve Smith, whose career has operated on a series by series basis for several years. World.title: Overdose suspected in Hayden Panettiere death as emergency audio emerges
World.content:
CultureCelebrityVale Overdose suspected in Hayden Panettiere death as emergency audio emerges Chris Hook and Nell Geraets August 18, 2026 — 7:39am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

No foul play is suspected in the death of American actor Hayden Panettiere, police said, as emergency dispatch audio published by several US outlets indicated the star was in cardiac arrest following a suspected overdose. The 36-year-old died at her South Carolina home on Monday (AEST). Hayden Panettiere in 2023. Her father announced her death on Monday. Getty Images Best known for her roles in TV shows Heroes and Nashville, her death was confirmed by her father Skip Panettiere in a statement to US media. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” he said. “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her – and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”



Related Article Updated

Vale Nashville star Hayden Panettiere dies at age 36 Early on Tuesday morning (AEST), Greenville Police said in a statement that emergency services were called to Panettiere’s home at 1.51pm on Sunday after she was found to be unresponsive by a friend. It remains unclear who made the 911 call. Medical assistance was given, but she was pronounced dead at the scene. “The preliminary investigation has not indicated any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances,” police said in the statement. The case is under investigation by the police department and the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.



“An autopsy was completed today. At autopsy, no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to the death,” the statement said. The Greenville County Coroner’s Office also confirmed Panettiere’s death, noting in a statement that she was “found unresponsive inside the residence where she had been temporarily staying”. Panettiere rose to fame in the TV series Heroes, before landing roles in Nashville, Scream 4 and the Bring It On series. Getty Responders reportedly “initiated advanced cardiac life support measures”, which can include breathing tubes, defibrillators and emergency intravenous medications. However, these efforts were unsuccessful, and Panettiere was pronounced dead at 2.32pm (local time). The official cause and manner of the actor’s death remain unknown, and would be determined following further investigation and “the completion of additional studies”, the coroner’s office said.



Related Video Video icon 2:07 Actress Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36 US outlet People reported that emergency workers were heard discussing an “overdose” and “cardiac arrest” in dispatch audio obtained by the publication and other outlets including TMZ. According to several US reports, the actor flew out of Los Angeles with her on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson the day before she died. It remains unclear whether Hickerson was the friend who found her unresponsive on Monday (AEST). Panettiere died a few days before her 37th birthday, which would have been on Friday. She began her acting career at the age of four, with a role in the soap opera One Life to Live as Sarah Roberts. She was perhaps best recognised as Claire Bennet in the popular sci-fi series Heroes, and as Juliette Barnes in Nashville. She also had various film roles including in Remember the Titans and Scream 4. This year, she released a memoir titled This Is Me: A Reckoning. In it, she recounted the impact of being a child actor, her past alcohol addiction and giving up custody of her daughter in 2018.



Panettiere entered an in-patient treatment centre in early 2020 where she worked on overcoming her opioid and alcohol addiction. Though she remained largely out of the spotlight for a few years, Panettiere re-emerged in May to promote her memoir. World.title: ‘The money will come’: Why Pritchard brothers turned down PNG riches to stay in rugby
World.content:
Exclusive SportRugby UnionWallabies ‘The money will come’: Why Pritchard brothers turned down PNG riches to stay in rugby Jonathan Drennan August 18, 2026 — 7:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Before making the biggest decision of their young professional careers, Treyvon and Kadin Pritchard thought back to two important lessons taught to them by their parents, Daniel and Brenda: never leave a job half done, and always show loyalty to those who backed you from the start. The brothers ultimately turned down the lucrative offer tabled by the PNG Chiefs to join the NRL expansion franchise for its inaugural season in 2028, opting instead to remain at their respective rugby clubs, with Treyvon signing an extension with the Reds until 2029 and Kadin remaining at the Brumbies until 2030. Both brothers also have the opportunity to play sevens in the 2028 Olympics. Treyvon (L) and Kadin Pritchard are staying in Australian rugby. Rugby Australia “I think from a young age mum and dad have always instilled in us the value of finishing what you’ve started and never doing a half job,” Treyvon told this masthead. “Our parents taught us to finish what we’ve started. Loyalty does come into play, too. It’s a big part of our everyday lives and something that our parents have made us follow, and it’s led into our everyday life.



“Also, coming through from being a 15-year-old in the Reds environment to moving up and training with the older boys while I was still in school with a couple of my mates. “We all have come through at the same time and we have those connections, and I think a big thing with footy is being able to trust your teammates. If you already have something in place, there’s no real reason to kind of change that and switch it up. Treyvon is one of the most exciting talents in Australian rugby. World Rugby “So I think the friendships and the connections that I already have are also a big part of my reasoning to stay in Australian rugby.” The brothers spoke highly of their dealings with the Chiefs, but ultimately turned down the lucrative offer because they felt they have unfinished business in rugby together – and believe the money will follow them eventually.



“Obviously, it was exciting [to get the PNG offer] and yeah, we did meet with them, and I think that was probably both our first real kind interest from league. So we tested the waters and we were trying to see what it was all about,” Treyvon said. “But I think Rugby Australia had a lot to offer as well. Like I said before, loyalty played a big part in where we are now and that helped us to a decision on where we wanted to be for the next couple of years... “The money is going to come, it’s probably not the biggest worry at the moment. We need to focus on establishing ourselves in our respective teams.” Kadin said that beyond immediate financial rewards, rugby will offer the brothers a chance to travel the world while playing the game they love. “I love rugby union and the possibilities that it can bring with the worldwide game were a big thing for me to stay here,” Kadin said.



“To travel around the world, playing international teams – and even if it’s club level, you can go over somewhere like France. The possibilities of doing that sort of thing, you don’t get that in other sports.” The Ella brothers brought an almost telepathic understanding to the Wallabies back line in the 1980s and the Pritchards believe they can eventually replicate that synergy as a centre partnership for the Australian Test team. Kadin Pritchard dreams of forming a centre partnership with Treyvon at Test level for the Wallabies . Getty Images “It’s definitely a dream of ours to link up at some point,” Kadin said. “We’ve been separated for a reason: to build ourselves up in our own teams and build the groups around us. “By the time we get to the Wallabies, we’ll be set to go, because we’ve got that brother intuition ... we want to play together in the centres, with Trayvon at inside centre.



“It’s definitely been a thought in my mind becoming that 12 and 13, and you probably don’t see it too often having brothers in the centres with that connection. We’re just almost interlinked and we know how each other plays from doing it so often in the backyard.” Having spent endless hours playing together as kids, the two brothers came up against each other for the first time last season, when the Reds faced the Brumbies in Super Rugby. But Treyvon says it is when playing together on the same side that their close relationship brings an extra edge. “We probably don’t have to speak as much as other players would; we can communicate with our body language and trust is a big factor in the connection that we have over other players,” Treyvon said. At 22 years old, Kadin has always felt protective of Treyvon, who is three years younger than him. Treyvon affectionately calls Kadin the family’s “test dummy”, the older brother who had to forge the way into professional rugby before passing on the lessons learned along the way. Though separated by distance, the brothers still speak regularly and operate as a unit when it comes to making decisions on their rugby future.



The brothers have been brought up to support one another, wary that there will always be others outside the family who want to tear one or another of them down. “We know what each other can do and why should we hate on our family when you’ve got haters outside already,” Kadin said. “The tightness of our family, it’s just been brought through by our dad. Treyvon Pritchard suffered serious injuries in this hip drop tackle against Wales at the Junior World Championship, but is recovering well after surgery. Stan Sport “We’re our own biggest supporters, we’ve got to support each other and build each other up so there’s no hate coming from within, and we have a support group here. “There’s no way I’m going to hate on what my bro’s doing. I’m just going to hype him up to be the best player in the world. What’s the point of trying to pull him down when everybody else is trying to do that?”



Both brothers are currently recovering from injuries. Kadin is nursing a hamstring strain but hopes to return to play for the Brumbies in the Super Rugby AUS competition, while Treyvon is recovering from an operation after breaking his right leg ain a hip drop tackle while representing Australia Under 20s. Treyvon’s current recovery timeline is between 12 and 18 weeks. Related Article Australian rugby ‘Run us off our feet’: Wallabies’ surprising ploy to prepare for Japanese heat Both brothers are focused on establishing their positions with their respective Super Rugby clubs ahead of a new season, but Treyvon is aware there will always be future possibilities, whether in rugby or the NRL. “We’re definitely not closed off to playing overseas, and I think once we make a decision on that, I think we would probably look to play together, I don’t see why we wouldn’t,” Treyvon said. “I think living in a different country is hard enough, so I think being with the older bro would be awesome. “I’m [also] not closed off to the NRL. Obviously all the noise that’s been happening recently probably sparked a bit of interest for everyone, but it’s definitely an option down the track. I’m with the Reds for three years and with Aussie rugby for three years, so whatever happens after that happen.” News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

World.title: ASX set to slide, Wall Street retreats as oil prices climb; BHP, CSL results ahead
World.content:
Updated BusinessMarketsWorld markets ASX set to slide, Wall Street retreats as oil prices climb; BHP, CSL results ahead Stan Choe Updated August 18, 2026 — 6:24am ,first published 5:22am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

US stocks edged further from their record heights on Monday after rising oil prices cranked up the pressure on inflation and financial markets. The S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent but remains near its all-time high set Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 272 points, or 0.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.3 per cent. Wall Street opened the week with more losses. Bloomberg The Australian sharemarket is set to decline, with futures at 6.04am AEST pointing to a fall of 40 points, or 0.5 per cent, at the open. The ASX lost 0.5 per cent on Monday. The Australian dollar is stronger at US71.03¢. Reporting season continues with BHP and CSL results slated to be released today. Wall Street’s losses solidified in the afternoon when oil prices accelerated upward. The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, rose 2.7 per cent to $US90.87.



Related Article Exclusive

James Packer James Packer’s bets on AI pay off after sell-down in gaming shares It’s been careening back and forth because of uncertainty about what the war with Iran will do to the global flow of crude. Last month alone, Brent zigzagged between $US72 and $US102 as hopes rose and fell that the United States and Iran could reach a deal that would allow oil tankers to freely exit the Persian Gulf again. Monday’s rally for oil prices sent Treasury yields in the bond market higher, which in turn raised the pressure on the economy and prices for all kinds of investments. The yield on the 10-year Treasury climbed to 4.72 per cent from 4.68 per cent late Friday. It has shot up from just 3.97 per cent before the war with Iran, largely because higher oil prices are worsening inflation and upping the probability that the Federal Reserve will have to hike interest rates. Higher rates could keep a lid on inflation, but they do so by intentionally slowing the economy. The average long-term US mortgage rate has already jumped near its highest level in a year because of the rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, though reports last week said that inflation in July was not as bad as earlier in the summer.



Usually around this time of year, anticipation is building on Wall Street to hear from the head of the Federal Reserve about where it may take interest rates. But the Fed’s new chairman, Kevin Warsh, may give little insight at this year’s economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, at the end of this month, according to Thierry Wizman, a strategist at Macquarie Group Warsh has been adamant about giving Wall Street less guidance about the Fed’s plans for interest rates. Wall Street has run to records despite high inflation in large part because profits are booming for U.S. companies. Those in the S&P 500 index are on track to deliver growth of roughly 50 per cent for earnings per share in the spring from a year earlier, according to FactSet. That’s much better than analysts expected and would be the best since five years ago, when the economy was erupting out of the chasm created by the COVID pandemic. Nearly all the companies in the S&P 500 have turned in their profit reports for the spring. Still to come are big retailers, including reports this week from Home Depot, Target and Walmart.



Related Article Opinion

Trump's America Trump makes America Inc’s grip on the world even tighter They’re facing pressure. Their customers’ incomes may be turning iffier after U.S. employers surprisingly cut more jobs last month than they added. At the same time, their customers are continuing to see bills rise quickly as inflation remains much higher than anyone would like. A report last week said that shoppers surprisingly spent less at U.S. retailers last month than in June, and CEOs for retailers could give color this week on what they’re seeing. On Wall Street, trading was relatively quiet Monday. L3Harris Technologies fell 4.6 per cent after the defense company said Christopher Kubasik stepped down as its CEO and chairman following “certain conduct by Kubasik that was not consistent with the values of the Company.” It gave few details but said the conduct was not related to its financial reporting, controls, customer relationships or operational performance.



Alphabet dipped 0.5 per cent even though Berkshire Hathaway said it increased its investment in Google’s parent company, along with several homebuilders. Berkshire built a reputation for buying stocks at affordable prices under its former CEO, famed investor Warren Buffett. Constellation Brands fell 6.2 per cent after Berkshire said it sold all its holdings in the seller of Modelo beer and Robert Mondavi wine. All told, the S&P 500 fell 40.70 points to 7,745.06. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 272.63 to 53,459.78, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 84.25 to 26,644.91. In stock markets abroad, indexes dipped in Europe following a stronger finish in Asia. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.7 per cent after a report said Japan’s economy grew at a slower pace in the April-June quarter than economists expected. Indexes jumped 1.3 per cent in Hong Kong and 1.4 per cent in Shanghai for some of the world’s biggest moves.
