World.title: Vector profit jumps 55 percent as new pricing rules fund record network investment
World.content:
Vector has reported a 55 percent jump in annual profit after the first full year under new electricity pricing rules, while investing a record half a billion dollars in Auckland's power network.

Key numbers for the year ended June compared with a year ago:

Net profit $240.2m v $154.7m

Revenue $1.20b v $1.10b

Adjusted EBITDA $482.2m v $401.1m

Gross capital expenditure $544m v $469m

Final dividend 13.5 cents per share v 12.5 cents

Vector, the Auckland energy distribution company, has reported a 55 percent surge in net profit to $240.2 million, while underlying earnings rose 20 percent to $482.2 million, largely reflecting the first full year under the Commerce Commission's latest electricity distribution pricing reset.

Revenue from its electricity business rose 18 percent to $905 million, while natural gas distribution revenue increased 2 percent to $69 million.

The number of gas connections slipped 0.5 percent to just under 120,000.

The company connected more than 13,000 new homes and businesses to Auckland's electricity network during the year.

Chief executive Chris Blenkiron said a focus on customer outcomes, safety, and operational and financial performance had delivered a strong result.

Vector invested a record $512 million in Auckland's electricity network during the financial year to meet the needs of a growing population and an increasingly electrified economy.

"Demand continues to evolve as the city expands, while EVs, solar and other technologies reshape how existing customers use energy," Blenkiron said.

"We are carefully prioritising investment, improving how we plan and operate the network, and using new technologies to get more from existing infrastructure."

The board determined an unimputed final dividend of 13.5 cents per share, taking the full year dividend to 26 cents per share.

Vector is Auckland's electricity lines company, operating the region's electricity and gas distribution networks. Although listed on the NZX, it is majority-owned by consumer trust Entrust, which holds 75.1 percent of the shares.

World.title: Health NZ says cervical screening IT doesn't need overhaul
World.content:
Health New Zealand believes the technology behind its failure-prone cervical screening register is largely OK - but not entirely.

The register that was rushed in three years ago failed to trigger almost a million notifications to women about cancer screening.

Experts who investigated the problems last year told HNZ in February to look at whether the register's IT platform was viable and, if not, find other tech.

The agency's action plan says it will both assess and enhance the tech.

HNZ told RNZ it began that work in June.

"We are confident that the programme's IT system is generally fit for purpose, although we recognise there is work to do to ensure that invitations to screen are generated for all women that should get them," said national prevention screening director Alana Ewe-Snow.

"In short, we anticipate improvement to the current IT system, not an overhaul."

All 48 recommendations, including the tech to improve the system, would be completed within two years and it was monitoring for any harm meantime, HNZ said. No harm had been found.

Women's health advocates said the register failure was "appalling" and workforce churn, including at the tech level, had contributed to it.

As a result of the national screening unit being shut down as a standalone agency, data analysts had been shifted to HNZ's digital services side, helping create "exactly the kind of workforce churn that our organisations warned would be a recipe for disaster", said the Auckland Women's Health Council, Federation of Women's Health Councils and the Cartwright Collective in a statement.

The register was built to store cervical screening test results, track screening paths - how often women should be screened, according to risk - and send out notifications, including recalls, reminders and invitations to women.

Despite the failures, it had boosted screening numbers by just under 10 percent in 2023 to 77 percent in 2026, Ewe-Snow said.

"The register is working well for most women, so there is no intention to start again.

"We know, however, we have more work to do tighten the register to ensure invitations are getting sent to all eligible women."

The action plan says: "This includes enhancing digital and technology foundations."

Its launch in September 2023 was rushed, and HNZ knew it had limited functions and several problems, including incomplete data, yet did not monitor it properly after it went live, the expert investigation report's 118 pages found.

It was sending out only a couple of hundred notifications a week, instead of the expected few thousand.

By April 2024, an internal report showed the register's design was not up to expectations and the tech's 'logic' system "was not built as intended". Poor data quality made it worse.

That sparked the external review, done by mid-2025, although its report was released only this month, after reporting by Stuff.

"We are deeply concerned by reports that nurses and other frontline staff have said they tried to raise the alarm about these failings before the system went live," said the women's health advocates.

Initially, the project contract was signed in 2019, with Deloitte using software from Salesforce, although actual work began in 2022. By early 2023, it still needed funding.

The goalposts on technical requirements were shifted, as the screening platform was being built.

"The register is not yet functioning as a comprehensive clinical safety net," the review said in 2025, after 18 months of work trying to fix it.

It was, however, working "satisfactorily in many ways".

The advocates noted the failures included no screening histories properly transitioned onto the new register; and a "concerning level" of clinical risk around recommendation mismatches between screening laboratories and the register.

The experts gave Health NZ a list of five things to do on the tech front.

It "must critically assess the long-term viability of the register and the underlying National Screening Solution [NSS]", they said in February.

It needed to know from the IT supplier if and when this could be done, and at what cost - and if not, change tack.

"If this assessment determines that the required functionality cannot be implemented, a risk-assessment should be undertaken of procuring a new software solution in the long term, rather than continuing with the register and NSS."

Ewe-Snow said they began that in June, "assessing how the technology that sits in behind the register can be improved", and this was ongoing, although a timeline was not yet finalised.

"We need to be alert to opportunities for further improvement, especially in a world where technology is changing rapidly."

World.title: ACT proposes 'Working with Children' card to replace police checks
World.content:
The ACT Party is campaigning on introducing a 'Working with Children Card' to ensure people are properly and continually vetted.

ACT spokesperson for children Karen Chhour said anyone employed to work with children would need one of the cards, which account for criminal convictions, disciplinary findings, and other records.

"The Working with Children Card would give parents confidence that their children are in safe hands," she said.

"It follows the worker, is continuously monitored, considers additional relevant information, and replaces duplicated screening by individual organisations."

Currently, safety checks are carried out once every three years, Chhour said.

"This provides only a snapshot of a person at one point in time, with no consistent system for identifying risks that emerge between checks," Chhour said.

"The system ensures that cardholders are safe the whole time they work with children, not just up until a check was last completed."

Offences could see the holder's card suspended or revoked, with employers and relevant regulators notified.

Employers would no longer have to wait for the next three-year check to discover that a worker's circumstances have changed, Chhour said.

World.title: Transport Minister Chris Bishop defends commissioning another Auckland harbour crossing report
World.content:
Government looks into second harbour bridge Morning Report Download MP3 6m

The Transport Minister is defending commissioning another report on a second harbour crossing in Auckland.

More than $106 million has been spent on consultants and contractors to date, but there is still no plan for what should be built and how.

On Monday, Chris Bishop announced plans for a detailed business case due next year.

He told Morning Report on Tuesday that previous reports have answered the 'why,' and now it needs to answer the 'how.'

"This will be multiple billions of dollars, one of the biggest projects we've ever built in New Zealand, and it's really important we get it right. I think everyone would agree on that," Bishop said.

"So, all the expert advice on this from when you do a mega project from the Infrastructure Commission and from others is that you need to follow a proper, thorough process, and that's what we're doing.

"We're going to do a detailed business case. That will take a bit of time, but that will give Cabinet, whoever is in the Cabinet, whether it's us or another set of parties, that will give the Cabinet good decisions on how to make an informed decision, and that's what we're all about."

Bishop said the NTZA had done two investment cases into a bridge next to the existing one and also into a tunnel.

He said it looked at what's preferable to be built from engineering, network connectivity, and transport point of views.

Weekly interview with opposition leader, Chris Hipkins Morning Report Download MP3 7m

Bishop said if he had announced then they were building a tunnel, he'd be asked to explain how.

"You would say, 'well, how are you going to pay for it?' And then you'd say, 'how much is it going to cost?' And then you'd say, 'when's it going to start?' And then you'd say, 'how's it going to be delivered?'

"We need to answer all of those questions because they're completely legitimate questions that the government has, and we need to do that work, and that's what we're going to do," he said.

"I think we're taking a very thorough, evidence-led approach to this."

He said another report did "absolutely" not mean they were back at square one.

"People who are framing it like that are, frankly, being a bit misleading and a bit mischievous," he said.

"There's been a huge amount of work done over the last two years or so, and, frankly, over the last four years, this whole process actually started with an indicative business case kicked off by the previous government."

Bishop said in 2027, Cabinet would be in a position to decide on what to build and how to pay for it.

"Once we have that information in a package, there'll be a range of options we look at, we'll be able to make an informed decision," he said.

"My hope would be that whoever is in government does it on a cross-party basis, because this will span multiple parliaments and multiple governments, and we need to get it right.

"We're setting the project up for success now and taking an evidence-led approach, which everyone says we should do, and I hope that we will end up with a good outcome next year."

Government's made no progress on Auckland harbour crossing - Hipkins

But Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins said the government had made no progress on a new Auckland harbour crossing in three years.

Hipkins told Morning Report when he was prime minister in 2023, he announced NZTA had indicated a tunnel was its "emerging preferred option", and ordered a detailed business case.

"Effectively the government have announced the same thing again yesterday, which is that ... the likely preferred option is a tunnel, but that they'll also weigh up the potential for a bridge instead," he said.

"That's not really any progress on where we were three years ago."

The business case was necessary, Hipkins said - but he thought that's what was being completed over the last three years.

"It is important that you get a good, robust business case because we need to make sure that the choices that we make are the right choices, and that we're going to get good value for money for whatever spending that the government ultimately decides to spend."

Hipkins said if Labour was elected in November, it would support the business case continuing, and go from there.

Bishop said he was seeking bipartisan support on the project, and Hipkins said he was open to that.

World.title: Disputes Tribunal orders Kmart to pay Christchurch couple over contaminated sand
World.content:
Kmart to pay Christchurch couple $15k to cover asbestos costs Morning Report Download MP3 5m

Kmart has been ordered to pay thousands to a Christchurch couple whose toddlers played with asbestos-contaminated sand.

Last year, the retail giant was part of a nationwide recall of coloured play sand products, after they tested positive for tremolite - a form of asbestos associated with higher cancer risks at low exposure levels.

Elle Chrisp and David Dingwall took Kmart to the Disputes Tribunal, seeking re-imbursement for costs associated with asbestos contamination and future medical monitoring.

The Christchurch pair claimed $60,000 in total.

In a recent decision, the tribunal ordered Kmart to pay the family $15,185.42 to cover costs associated with asbestos testing and remediation.

It found the play sand purchased was unsafe, not fit for purpose and not of acceptable quality under the Consumer Guarantees Act.

Elle Chrisp says the family is very happy with the outcome of the tribunal's case. Supplied / Screenshot

Elle Chrisp said the family had bought 4kg of the sand and it was in their backyard where their three-year-old twins played with it.

But she said from time to time the sand would end up inside the house as well as it came in on their shoes and clothes.

"We had our sand independently tested, it came back with tremolite asbestos, we were phoned and the advice we were given was to evacuate our home immediately taking just the clothes on our back, nothing else, leaving everything behind."

That was because further environmental testing was needed to find out exactly where the asbestos contamination was, she said.

Fortunately the testing showed the contamination was limited to backyard area, she said.

Kmart signage at the Westfield St Lukes mall. RNZ / Cole Eastham-Farrelly

The family incurred a number of costs in this process, she said, including lab testing, having to dispose of a lot of items such as toys that were stored outside and remediation to make the outdoor area safe.

The family was also not able to use the outdoor area for 67 days until it was remediated, she said.

Chrisp said they took the case to the tribunal because the product was unsafe and that was what they wanted to establish.

"We weren't seeing that communicated anywhere, parents were told that they were overreacting, it was low risk, it was never low risk, it was never safe and that was what the decision came to."

She said she was pleased that Kmart had to attend the tribunal hearing.

"Because we did not have any engagement from them at all prior to going to the tribunal and that's why we were so thankful the disputes tribunal process existed because it put us on an even footing with a huge company who otherwise could have ignored us."

The tribunal process which doesn't use lawyers was great because it was built for ordinary people to be able to get a fair outcome, she said.

Chrisp said they were very happy with the outcome of their tribunal case.

"Ultimately for us it was wanting a public ruling that this is enforceable."

Referee Cynthia Hawes said the sand should not have been offered for sale.

"I do not think that any reasonable parent, acquainted with the fact that the moulding sand contained asbestos, and regardless of the quantity or proportion in the sand, would purchase it for his or her child to play with."

The claim for medical expenses was not allowed.

A Kmart spokesperson said the product recall was part of a broader industry issue.

"When the matter became known to us, we acted quickly by removing affected products from sale, issuing recall notices, and supporting customers with refunds and guidance on safely disposing of the products based on regulatory advice."

They said the company was reviewing the tribunal's decision.

"We remain focused on supporting our customers on this matter while being guided by evidence, expert advice and the relevant regulators."

Consumer NZ head of research and advocacy Gemma Rasmussen said Chrisp and Dingwall spent months gathering evidence, and forked out thousands of dollars to take Kmart to the Disputes Tribunal.

She said the ruling found "firmly in the family's favour".

"It is completely reasonable for them to undertake everything that they did from testing to vacating their home, and Kmart should have to pay for that."

Rasmussen said the ruling did not set a precedent, but it sent a clear message and she hoped other families were encouraged to make claims.

However, she said the order ultimately showed the difficulty in getting redress following a product safety failure.

She said current laws were too reactive and regulatory reform was needed.

"Our market place has dramatically changed from major retailers like Kmart selling thousands of goods to people shopping on platforms like Temu and Ali Express, and we really need the government to take this a little more seriously."

World.title: CNMI mayors warn of escalating meth crisis, ask for more DEA resources
World.content:
The Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands is experiencing a methamphetamine crisis, the four local mayors of the US territory have warned.

The mayors of Saipan, Rota, Tinian and Aguiguan, and the Northern Islands say local resources can no longer keep pace with the scale and sophistication of methamphetamine trafficking.

Saipan mayor Ramon "RB" Jose Blas Camacho, Rota mayor Aubry Hocog, Tinian and Aguiguan mayor Edwin Aldan, and Northern Islands Mayor Valentino Taisakan Jr have joined forces to request the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) to send additional agents and personnel.

The CNMI's local law enforcement agency, the Department of Public Safety (DPS), declined to weigh in on the mayors' request.

DPS acting public information officer Simon Manacop, speaking on behalf of DPS Commissioner Anthony Macaranas, told Marianas Press: "He will not provide a comment as the matter was not addressed to him nor was he consulted about it."

In a letter dated 10 August 2026, addressed to DEA Director Terrence Cole, the mayors described methamphetamine as an "urgent and escalating threat" to the health, safety and stability of CNMI communities and sought increased federal assistance.

"Methamphetamine trafficking and abuse have reached levels that our local enforcement and community-support systems can no longer sustain alone," the they wrote.

They said that despite the efforts of local police, community organisations and government agencies, the scale and sophistication of methamphetamine distribution networks operating in the CNMI have "outpaced our available manpower and resources".

The mayors said the consequences include rising addiction rates, increased property and violent crime, strained social services and the erosion of community well-being.

The mayors specifically asked DEA to deploy additional agents, analysts, and interdiction specialists who could work directly with local law enforcement.

They said additional federal personnel could strengthen intelligence gathering and investigative capacity, support joint operations targeting methamphetamine importation and distribution, and enhance interdiction efforts at ports of entry and along maritime routes.

World.title: Mercury Energy posts $1 billion in earnings on strong hydro generation
World.content:
Electricity company Mercury has posted record operating earnings as hydro generation improved and expenses fell.

The company's bottom line profit also rebounded strongly after last year's results were affected by one-offs.

Key numbers for the 12 months ended June compared with a year ago:

Net profit after tax $321m v $1m

Revenue $3.22b v $3.5b

Operating earnings (EBITDAF) $1.07b v $786m

Operating expenses $370m v $396m

Generation 9070 GWh v 7906 GWh

Final dividend 17 cents per share v 14.4 cps

Operating earnings (the preferred earnings measure) rose 36 percent to a record $1.07 billion, the first time Mercury has exceeded the $1b mark, and came in above guidance.

Alongside strong hydro generation, three new projects began generating power during the year. The new assets were a mix of geothermal expansion and new wind farms.

Mercury said strong inflows into the Waikato catchment lifted hydro generation 31 percent from a year earlier.

The company said it reinvested 66 percent of its 2026 financial year operating earnings in new and existing renewable generation assets.

Mercury chief executive Stew Hamilton. Supplied/Mercury

"We are converting strong financial performance into new generation, greater system resilience and the capacity to support New Zealand's future economic growth," chief executive Stew Hamilton said.

The company said its next development would be Puke Kapo Hau wind farm, west of Dunedin. The project would support South Island demand, including from Datagrid NZ, a company planning to build a massive data centre in Southland.

Mercury recently announced a $53 million investment in Datagrid NZ.

"Datagrid shows how long-term demand, renewable development and disciplined investment can work together," Hamilton said.

World.title: OFC Pro League prepares for its second season
World.content:
Season 2 of the Oceania Football Confederation Pro-League (OFC Pro-League) will begin in February 2027.

The eight clubs who made up the inaugural 2026 competition received approval for their 2027 Club Licence applications.

Auckland FC beat South Melbourne 2-1 in the inaugural final of the 2026 OFC Pro League competition in May.

"Reaching Season 2 is an important moment for the OFC Pro League and for the continued development of professional football in the region," OFC Pro League head Stuart Larman said.

"Having all eight clubs approved at this stage reflects the commitment they have made to meeting the standards required to operate at this level. This is about more than simply preparing for another season - it is about building strong, sustainable independent clubs that can contribute to the future of football across Oceania.

"We now look forward to working closely with the clubs as they complete the remaining participation requirements and prepare for what promises to be another exciting chapter for the league."

The eight clubs set to continue in the second year of the OFC Pro League are Auckland FC and South Island United from New Zealand, South Melbourne from Australia, Bula FC (Fiji), Hekari FC (Papua New Guinea), Solomon Kings FC (Solomon Islands), Tahiti United (Tahiti) and Vanuatu United FC (Vanuatu).

World.title: LIV Golf ending season early after cancelling final event
World.content:
LIV Golf is ending its season one week earlier than planned, announcing on Monday it will not hold the team championship in Michigan next week and instead crown the team champion this week.

The 12 events this year — New Orleans was previously postponed — are the smallest schedule for LIV since it was launched with massive Saudi Arabian funding and eight tournaments in 2022.

Jon Rahm has already clinched the individual season title for the third straight year. LIV Golf Indianapolis, which starts on Thursday at The Club at Chatham Hills, will determine who finishes second and third among the players, and the top team.

Embattled LIV Golf tour asks to defer payment to Adelaide golf club The future of LIV Golf Adelaide has been further "shrouded in doubt", the SA opposition says, after LIV asked for an extension on a payment to Kooyonga Golf Club, which is scheduled to host the event next year.

The Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, the financial muscle of the rival league from the start, decided in March this would be the final year of funding.

LIV Golf announced earlier this month it had an agreement with a lead investor that would sustain a new version of the league for 2027.

"By concluding the season now, we can put our full resources behind what comes next and maintain the operational rigor this transition demands," LIV CEO Scott O'Neil said in a statement.

"We are reimagining LIV Golf as a fundamentally new league owned by the players and anchored in a sustainable business model, with an evolved fan experience built for the markets where the game is growing fastest across the globe and the support of world-class partners."

The cancellation of LIV Golf Michigan was not surprising.

There have been reports in recent weeks the tournament had not even started preparing with grandstands and other amenities. LIV Golf said ticket holders would get refunds.

In another cost-cutting move LIV attributed to "unavoidable changes in the entertainment program", the league informed Thomas Rhett and Disco Lines their live performances would not take place at LIV Golf Indianapolis.

The final event, with a $US20 million ($28.1 million) purse that pays $US4 million to the winner, could be the last big pay-off for LIV and its 57 players.

LIV did not identify the lead investor or how much of a cash infusion was involved, or say whether it was an investment or a loan.

O'Neil has said the LIV 2.0 version for 2027 and onward would involve making players equity owners. He referred to it as a "second bite at the apple" being equity instead of cash.

But this likely is the end of $US20 million purses for individual outcomes, and there have already been cutbacks. Rahm earned $US6 million for winning the points title, down from $US18 million the previous two years.

"As we concentrate on finishing the season strong and building the next chapter of LIV Golf, we'll carry the energy and enthusiasm our fans have shown us into what comes next," O'Neil said.

The format for the 2027 season and the rosters also remain unclear.

Still to be determined is whether Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau — the two biggest names — and other players who joined the league for its exorbitant prize money will want to stay for LIV 2.0.

As for the final event, Joaquin Niemann, Lucas Herbert and Tyrrell Hatton are in the mix for third place, which pays a $US1 million bonus. DeChambeau is comfortably in second, which pays $US3 million.

Dustin Johnson's 4Aces team has a narrow lead over Australia-based Ripper, with Rahm's Legion XIII and Bryson DeChambeau's Crushers team all in the mix for the team title.

AP

World.title: FIFA executive who criticised Infantino's World Cup sale plan departs
World.content:
FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, has left soccer's governing body, weeks after he publicly criticised president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell a stake in its tournament business, including the World Cup.

"FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA's chief operating officer has ended on 17 August 2026," a FIFA spokesperson said.

How Gianni Infantino's FIFA leadership imploded over two weeks The FIFA president has faced more than a fortnight of international turmoil, embroiled in a World Cup sell-off saga that sparked loss of confidence in his leadership.

"FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future. No further comment will be made on the matter."

Lamour had publicly criticised the proposal last month, saying FIFA staff had been "deceived" over the plan and describing it as "the project of one person".

"Our mission … is to serve football. Not to serve the personal interests of a person who, unfortunately, believes he embodies FIFA when he is supposed to be at its service," Lamour said in a statement at the time.

Lamour's comments came hours after Carlos Cordeiro, a senior adviser to Infantino, resigned in protest at the proposal, calling it "a bad deal for football".

The internal dissent came as FIFA faced widespread opposition to its plan to create a $US20 billion ($28.1 billion) subsidiary to run its tournaments, including the World Cup, and sell up to a 20 per cent stake to external investors. FIFA subsequently abandoned the proposal following the backlash.

Reuters

World.title: Why this future star has 'goosebumps' over triathlon's future
World.content:
The future of triathlon in Australia is looking very bright — particularly on the Gold Coast.

And 19-year-old rising star Aspen Anderson is hoping to play a big part in that future.

Last week, AusTriathlon formally opened its new high performance hub at the Miami Aquatic Centre, a home for the sport's best athletes and coaches, as well as the future, developing talent through the Ascent Academy.

It's a move that positions the Gold Coast right at the heart of the multi-sport universe leading into the 2032 Olympics.

The proposed location of the triathlon events at those Brisbane Games is the Gold Coast, and that is something that has Australia's top athletes very excited.

Aspen Anderson says knowing that a friendly, smiling face will be there at the new high performance hub was motivating. (Getty Images: Commonwealth Sport/Kevin C. Cox)

"I think having a home, for a home Olympics is really special," Anderson told ABC Sport on the Gold Coast.

"Sometimes it [training] is a bit of a slog when you have to put the headphones in and you're just trying to get it done.

"But knowing that there's always someone that can go for a ride with you, yeah, it definitely helps.

"It's like a strength in numbers kind of thing. Some days when you're not feeling great, they're always there to lift you up and someone's always got a smile on their face, and on your hard days, they might be having a great day, and vice versa, when you're having a good day, you can help a friend out too.

"This hub is definitely a great step forward, it's been hard in previous years where you're kind of just floating between venues. Now, having this locked in is really exciting."

Aspen Anderson has an athletics background and competed in the Women's U20s race during the 2023 World Cross Country Championships. (Getty Images: World Athletics/Cameron Spencer)

Reigning World Champion Matt Hauser agreed, saying the hub was a huge step forward for the athletes.

"For sure I wouldn't be able to do this sport if I was just training solo, seven days a week across the three sports," Hauser told ABC Sport.

"I think it's a really important dynamic that you also get that racing exposure in training and you're able to push each other and go to another level than you would have previously without someone there pushing you.

"Having that culture piece, having everyone on the same path and knowing that when you're putting the hard yards in, when your heart rate's maxing out, when you've got a sore body at the end of the week, everyone's in the same position and they're motivated to get to the same place as you are is, I think, really important, especially when we move towards Brisbane 2032.

"Everyone wants success for the country … so to be on that journey together and have that centralised program here in Miami now is, I think, really powerful."

Anderson noted that Hauser has "led the way" in bringing Australia back to the top step of world triathlon.

The 28-year-old claimed the world title on home soil in Wollongong last year, becoming the first Australian since Emma Moffatt in 2010.

It put Australia back on top of the triathlon world after a lengthy absence, and with the global hiring of new high performance coaches like British former European champion Non Stanford-Royle and Germany's former world champion Daniel Unger, hopes are that Hauser's success will be just the latest in a long line of triumphs.

Anderson herself is clearly on the right pathway to emulating some of the greats of the past.

Aspen Anderson won two gold medals at the 2023 Youth Commonwealth Games in Trinidad and Tobago. (Getty Images: Commonwealth Sport/Kevin C. Cox)

A double gold medallist from the Youth Commonwealth Games in Trinidad and Tobago in 2023, the Victoria-born teenager made her World Triathlon Championship Series debut earlier this season.

At the event in Quiberon, France, in June, Anderson led off Australia's mixed team relay to a sensational fourth place finish.

"I was really fortunate to get to experience the mixed team relay," Anderson said.

"I loved it. It was so fun, it's short enough that you're still with all the best of the best, like I'm lining up next to [Luxemburg's European champion] Jeanne Lehair and [French mixed team relay world championship gold medallist] Emma Lombardi, and I'm like 'wow, these are people that are performing on the biggest stages and here I am, just hey guys'.

"I had a bit of a fangirl moment but it was a great experience."

Aspen Anderson first took up triathlons in high school. (Getty Images: Commonwealth Sport/Kevin C. Cox)

Fresh from that fourth place, a couple of weeks later Anderson made her full individual World Championship Series debut in Hamburg, finishing 38th as the second-youngest of all the competitors in the race.

"I wasn't even planning to do World Series races this year, that was not even really on the cards, and then I think I just had a little bit too much momentum and they were like, 'oh, let's just go for it,'" Anderson said.

"Hamburg was another extreme … the crowds and everything, it was insane.

"It was definitely a big step up but it wasn't as big as everyone made it seem, I think maybe I over-hyped it a little bit in my head.

"But now I know what it's like and I know what to expect for next time. Every race is different though, so you never know what to expect."

Anderson will race in Weihai, China, at the end of the month, and has also been named to the Australian under 23 squad for the 2026 World Triathlon Championship Finals in Pontevedra, Spain, later this year.

This too came somewhat as a surprise for a teenager well and truly on the fast-track to the top.

It's made the prospect of a home Olympics all the more tantalising.

Anderson cites Cassandre Beaugrand's victory in Paris as being a huge inspiration. (Getty Images: Lars Baron)

"It's always something in the back of your mind," Anderson said.

"I'm someone that's really realistic, so I don't want to get ahead of myself, I'm kind of taking it race by race or day by day and really enjoying the process of doing that.

"But yeah, there's some days where you just get goosebumps thinking about it, just, wow there's an Olympics literally out the front door; there's talks of it being in Tallebudgera or Currumbin, and if it's in Currumbin that's literally where I live, so that would be something you could write in a fairytale ending.

"Cassie [Beaugrand, Paris 2024 Olympic champion] and what she did at her home Olympics, I think it's … yeah it literally is giving me goosebumps now thinking about it.

"Having the support of a home base going for something like 2032 is insane — and LA would be a lovely stepping stone for that, it would be lovely just to dip the toes in the water and still be competitive and then I think, yeah, it would be lovely to have a fairytale ending in Brisbane."

World.title: Options slim for new Australia Test cricket batters
World.content:
Australia's nine-wicket defeat at the hands of Bangladesh has thrown up yet more questions about the state of Australian batting.

Twin failures by opener Jake Weatherald and number three Marnus Labuschagne have only increased the pressure on both batters.

Moreover, the repeated failures of the batting line-up, with the exception of Steve Smith and Cam Green in Darwin, have continued a pattern which was partially masked by last season's Ashes success.

Shock loss to Bangladesh reveals Aussie cracks On paper, Australia's full-strength team should have wiped the floor with Bangladesh. But a lack of application to their Test match craft has left Australia vulnerable to teams that are driven to succeed in the longest format.

Labuschagne has not scored a century since July 2023 — 22 Tests ago — during which time he has averaged just 25.23.

Jake Weatherald is averaging 20.36 in his six Tests since the beginning of the Ashes last summer, with just one score above 50.

The question is, does Australia make changes now ahead of the second Test starting in Mackay on Saturday?

Skipper Pat Cummins openly mused on the subject in his post-Test press conference on Sunday.

"I think that's the question over the next couple days," Cummins said.

"We'll sit down and have a think; the selectors will have a think.

"Is there something there that's going to take us forward, or is it something starting to become a trend that we think needs to be changed?

"So, it's trying to work out, do you need to intervene now, or do you let it play out and think [the current group] is the way forward?"

Pat Cummins is searching for answers after the disaster in Darwin. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Australia's head coach, Andrew McDonald, said the disastrous display in Darwin was clearly not good enough.

"Call it a trend, call it what you will, we believe our players are better than what they're putting out there at the moment," he said.

"And that falls on us as coaches as well; our job is to get the best out of playing group.

"I think if you go back to the original squad [of 13] that was picked, it was quite skinny.

"I think Bailes, George [head selector, George Bailey] left it very open as to you know, we could add depending on what we saw going through."

The obvious problem is that we are in the middle of winter season and most batsmen last played first-class cricket around five months ago.

It means the selectors do not have recent form to go off and so any decision about bringing in a player from outside the squad of 13 is going to rely on hunch as much as hard facts.

If it is the current group, the only other batter available in the squad is Josh Inglis, who scored 100 on debut against Sri Lanka in January 2025 but was dropped after his fifth Test during last summer's Ashes series.

Josh Inglis has had some time in the Test team, with varied success. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Inglis last represented Australia in the white ball format playing one-day internationals and T20 matches on the tour to Bangladesh in June.

The 31-year-old wicketkeeper-batter played five matches in this year's IPL for the Lucknow Super Giants, scoring 266 runs at an average of 53.2 and a strike rate of 186.

Inglis opens for Australia in the short forms of the game but has not batted higher than four in Test cricket and bats in the middle order for Western Australia in the Sheffield Shield.

Is he the long-sought-after answer to open for Australia? His record and usual batting position suggests not.

If not Inglis, then the selectors will have to look outside the current squad where pundits are putting forth names including Matthew Renshaw, Sam Harper, Nathan McSweeney, Cooper Connolly, Campbell Kellaway, Sam Konstas and Kurtis Patterson.

Queenslander Renshaw was part of the wider squad that trained in Brisbane before the Sri Lanka series and is a possibility to replace Weatherald as opener.

Matthew Renshaw has played successfully as an opener for Australia. (Getty: Robert Cianflone)

He scored 499 runs in six matches at 49.9 in last year's Sheffield Shield, with three centuries and a 50.

While those numbers do not scream "pick me", they are actually a stand-out in what was a disappointing summer for Australia's first-class batters: his average was second only to Jack Edwards's 51.75 for batters who scored more than 300 runs.

Former Test opener and Queenslander Matthew Hayden is a fan of the 31-year-old.

"I want to see Matt Renshaw and I've been saying this for at least 12 months. I think he is match-fit," he told Channel 7.

"I think the selectors knew what he was, now I want to see what he actually is."

Renshaw was also a member of the Australian side that played limited overs matches against Bangladesh in June.

He played the last of his 14 Tests against India in Delhi more than three years ago when he came in as a concussion sub for David Warner and scored just 2.

Victoria's keeper/batter Sam Harper scored the second most Shield runs last year behind his teammate and former Test player, Peter Handscomb.

Sam Harper has batted well for Victoria, but can he step up to Test cricket? (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Harper scored 677 runs at an average 35.63 in his 11 matches, which included Victoria's loss to South Australia in the Sheffield Shield final played at the end of March.

Of late, 29-year-old Harper has been part of the Galle Gallants title-winning side in Sri Lanka's T20 competition, the Lanka Premier League.

He was the second-highest-scoring batter in the competition with 425 runs at an average of 38.63 and a strike rate of 163.46.

The question around Harper, who has proven himself a successful T20 batter over the years, is whether he could translate last year's Shield runs to the Test arena, and possibly even step up a level?

One player who has been playing regular first-class cricket is the former Test opener, Nathan McSweeney.

Nathan McSweeney was tried, briefly, at the top of the order. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

McSweeney was drafted into the Test side two years ago to replace the retired David Warner partnering Usman Khawaja at the top of the order.

He lasted just three Tests, where he made 72 runs at an average of 14.4.

More recently he has been playing for Northamptonshire in England's One-Day Cup and County Championship Division Two.

His record in eight first-class matches for Northants has been solid, scoring 589 runs — placing him fifth on the run-scoring charts — at an average of 49.08.

Batting at number three, he captained South Australia to last season's Sheffield Shield title and, at 27, he has added leadership qualities, more experience and maturity since he last played for Australia.

Cooper Connolly is the other former Test player who has been mentioned in dispatches.

Cooper Connolly is an option for the future. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Connolly played his one and only Test in Sri Lanka, where he batted at eight scoring four runs.

He has not played a first-class match since last March — one of four he played for Western Australia — scoring 216 runs in total with a top score of 70 and an average of 30.85.

He was part of the Australian team on the limited overs tour of Bangladesh, highlighted by his man of the match performance in the third ODI, where he scored 149 as an opener alongside Inglis.

Earlier in the year he scored 107 off just 59 balls for Punjab Kings in the Indian Premier League to become the youngest ever overseas centurion in that competition.

The Western Australian will turn 23 this year and so has youth on his side and is sure to play a part in Australia's Test side in the future.

The question is: Is he ready now?

Another youngster whose name keeps coming up is Victoria's Campbell Kellaway, who scored 509 runs in the last Shield season with one century and two 50s at an average of 26.78.

Campbell Kellaway gives another potential option as a prolific run-scorer at Shield level. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Kellaway was a member of the Cricket Australia XI that beat Bangladesh by an innings in a warm-up match in Darwin before the first Test.

Unfortunately, he was bowled for a duck off five balls.

Another young gun, Sam Konstas, has failed to grab his chances at the highest level.

The New South Welshman is unbelievably still only 20 but seems to have packed more into his brief career than many more senior players.

The five Tests he played following his dynamic Boxing Day debut against India two years ago have netted Konstas 163 runs at an average of 16.3.

Like Kellaway, he failed in the recent tour match against Bangladesh, scoring one.

Sam Konstas has already had a couple of memorable moments in his career. (AAP: Bianca De Marchi)

Konstas is a constant in the selectors' sights with a credible 660 runs in last season's Sheffield Shield at an average of 33.

The issue seems to be taming the impetuosity and proving he has the temperament to grind out a Test innings.

The forgotten man in Australian cricket is 33-year-old Kurtis Patterson.

Patterson scored 619 runs for NSW in the last Shield season at an average of 36.41.

His two Tests against Sri Lanka in 2019 included a not-out century but he was a victim of timing, squeezed out of the side as David Warner and Steve Smith returned from bans following the sandpaper scandal.

Patterson was a member of the CA XI, scoring 53 batting at number three which shows he's still in the thinking of selectors.

World.title: Golf course in court as parklands protesters take on SA government
World.content:
In what's been described as a David and Goliath battle, a trial has begun in the Federal Court, with two South Australians challenging the state government's redevelopment of the North Adelaide golf course.

Public servant Edwin Kemp Attrill and Kaurna Arabana woman Janette Milera are challenging the redevelopment, arguing it is in breach of federal conservation laws.

In front of other protesters opposed to the parklands project outside court, Mr Kemp Attrill said the unfolding legal process was "very nerve-wracking".

"It's a big uphill battle for us but we're really proud to be standing here," he said.

Ms Milera said she was taking action because she thought it was the right thing to do.

"This case is about respecting cultural tradition and truth telling," she said.

For [SA Premier] Peter [Malinauskas], it's a new golf course. For me, it's a bloodline.

"This case we're doing is because the parklands belong to the people and they need to be protected."

Protesters opposed to the state government's actions in the Adelaide parklands gathered outside the Federal Court. (ABC News: Leah MacLennan)

The state government announced its plan to redevelop and expand the golf course, as part of its bid to move the LIV Golf tournament into the city.

It said 585 trees would be cut down in the process, to be replaced with new plantings.

The state government passed laws earlier this year, taking control of that part of the parklands away from the Adelaide City Council, to allow it to go ahead with the redevelopment.

But the removal of trees sparked protests and the legal action taken by Mr Kemp Attrill and Ms Milera.

The redevelopment of the North Adelaide course has involved the felling of hundreds of trees. (ABC News: Lincoln Rothall)

In his opening address, the lawyer for the pair, Arturo Dal Cin, told the court the Adelaide parklands were given national heritage listing in 2008.

He said more than 400 trees had already cut down at the golf course — a number he said accounted for 15 per cent of all the trees in the area marked for the first stage of the development.

"Recognition of parklands necessarily includes recognition of established trees, because a necessary element of parklands is established, mature trees," Mr Dal Cin said.

He said the works have impacted the national heritage values of the parklands.

"A fundamental issue in this case, one of the fundamental issues, is the extent to which your Honour finds the removal of trees to this scale to be a significant impact on what the appellants will be contending is a national heritage value — namely the parklands and their protection," he said.

Trees were removed from the area in May. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

Mr Dal Cin said evidence would also be presented during the trial about the impact on Aboriginal cultural heritage and on local flying fox populations.

'Assault on democracy'

Before going to court, government lawyers wrote to Mr Kemp Attrill, warning him he could be liable for $4 million in costs if he lost.

Outside court, Mr Kemp Attrill said the government had not backed down.

"It's really concerning to us that in a public interest case the government has continued to say that they will essentially crush us if they win," he said.

"We think that's incredibly unfair and it's an assault on democracy in South Australia."

Mr Kemp Attrill had submitted an affidavit to the court saying he was "shocked" when he saw the loss of trees.

On cross-examination, he was shown aerial pictures of the course before and after the tree removal.

Crown lawyer Alison Doecke KC asked if a significant number of trees remained in the parklands following the works.

"I put to you that when one has regard to the aerial view, it is very hard to identify where the trees have been removed," she said.

"From the two photographs, yes," Mr Kemp Attrill said.

He said he often walks his dog around the golf course at night, and he has noticed the loss of trees.

"Walking around the perimeter, you can notice there's more sky," he said.

The redevelopment of the course was announced as part of plans for LIV Golf. (ABC News: Che Chorley)

Ms Doecke suggested to Mr Kemp Attrill that "the significant change in the appearance of the site is because of the removal of the grass, not the removal of the trees. Do you accept that?" she said.

"No, as I said, it was noticeable as soon as the trees were removed; the view was different," Mr Kemp Attrill said.

"Standing outside the fence, if you're not right up against the fence you actually don't see the grass, you can only see the trees, and that was a noticeable difference."

But when asked by Ms Doecke if he would concede "there's still an awful lot of trees on the site", Mr Kemp Attrill said "yes".

Speaking at a media conference, Premier Peter Malinauskas said his government has acted lawfully.

"All the advice that I've received from the relevant agencies is they've sought to comply with all requirements as they've gone through it," he said.

" I've said all along that any individual is welcome to take up their rights to challenge things in court, as is being done in this particular instance. "

The trial is expected to take five days, with government lawyers to present their response on Wednesday.

World.title: Sydney Swans CEO confirms police investigating alleged incident 'involving several players'
World.content:
The Sydney Swans have confirmed several of their footballers were involved in an "alleged incident" in Melbourne last night.

The Swans issued a statement just after midday today.

"The Swans have notified the AFL and relevant authorities and cannot provide further comment at this stage," the club said.

Victoria Police separately issued a statement saying detectives were investigating a report of a sexual assault in East Melbourne.

The Sydney Swans stayed at the Pullman in East Melbourne last night. (ABC News)

"The incident occurred at a hotel on Wellington Parade in the early hours of the morning," a spokesperson said.

"The exact circumstances are yet to be established, and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing."

Sydney Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich called a press conference this afternoon that lasted less than one minute.

"We're still piecing together exactly what's transpired here and have our own set of internal inquiries ongoing," he said.

"Safe to say, we're extremely shocked and disappointed that this has taken place and that the players have found themselves in this situation.

"We understand the level of interest in the matter, and there's going to be lots of speculation, but given it's a police matter right now, that's all that we can say."

Matthew Pavlich addressed the media this afternoon. (ABC News)

The AFL released a brief statement.

"The club made the AFL aware of the matter which is currently under Victoria Police investigation," the statement read.

NSW Police Minister Yasmin Catley said she was unaware of the details of the allegations, but she was confident Victorian authorities would take them "very seriously."

"We have to be mindful of the fact that the alleged offences occurred in a different jurisdiction. So, they [Victoria Police] will be leading that investigation," she said.

Asked if she would be seeking a briefing from police herself given it was a high-profile case allegedly involving Sydney-based AFL players, she said: "The police will definitely lead on that" and "brief me accordingly".

"The investigation is underway, I think we should let the police do their work in Victoria, and the NSW police will let me know if I need to know anything."

The Swans were staying in Melbourne overnight after their 36-point win over Essendon at the MCG yesterday.

Sydney is sitting in second spot on the AFL ladder heading into the final round of the 2026 season, with the finals due to start within weeks.

The team has had 17 wins this season and is due to play its next game at home at the SCG against North Melbourne.

World.title: No smiles as Chris O'Connell advances, while Aussie women's campaign ends
World.content:
Chris O'Connell and Adam Walton have made it four Australian men in the third round of the Cincinnati Master, while Talia Gibson's loss to Aryna Sabalenka left the women's draw without green and gold representation.

Gibson was beaten 6-2, 7-6(7/2) by the world number one in an hour and 52 minutes, while O'Connell and Walton joined Alex de Minaur and Rinky Hijikata in the round of 32.

But O'Connell was in no mood to celebrate after progressing thanks to an injury retirement by 11th-seeded opponent Casper Ruud.

The Australian qualifier picked up his fourth win in five days at the Masters 1000 tournament in what is proving his most profitable week of the season, but there were no smiles as he sympathised with Norway's three-time grand slam finalist on his concerning retirement after 64 minutes play.

Ruud had started well, moving into a 5-2 lead in the opening set, but the Sydneysider powered back to take the first set, sealing it 7-5 with an ace, as Ruud began to look in increasing discomfort with a back problem.

With Ruud leading the second set 2-1 on serve, the Norwegian world number 17 stretched for a wide serve and immediately decided enough was enough, going to the net to offer his hand to the Aussie.

Clearly with one eye on the US Open, where the main draw starts a week on Sunday, 2022 Flushing Meadows runner-up Ruud was not keen to take any risks.

For world number 129 O'Connell, it was the continuation of an excellent spell following his first-round victory over Poland's world number 68 Kamil Majchrzak.

He will next meet Brazilian teenage superstar Joao Fonseca, who defeated Botic van de Zandschulp 6-4, 7-6(7/2), and victory in that match would push O'Connell back to the verge of the world's top 100.

Talia Gibson's loss to Aryna Sabalenka leaves no Australian women in the Cincinnati singles draw. (Getty Images: Robert Prange)

Walton made it four Australians through to the third round along with Hijikata, who faces Jakub Mensik, and national number one Alex de Minaur, who meets British Wimbledon hero Arthur Fery.

Walton, the 27-year-old Queenslander currently ranked 98 in the world, overcame the 29th-seeded Peruvian Ignacio Buse 6-4, 6-3 in 72 minutes to set up a showdown with either American Ben Shelton, the eighth seed, or Jaime Faria of Portugal.

World.title: After constant chopping and changing, Green goes 'back to what worked'
World.content:
Cameron Green has delivered for a shell-shocked Australian side to give himself breathing space at number five, leading captain Pat Cummins to predict a long stint in one position in the batting line-up.

Green's 104 in the second innings of the nine-wicket loss to Bangladesh in Darwin was his first in Australia and also broke an 11-innings run without passing the half-century mark.

The 27-year-old all-rounder has been heavily criticised in Australian cricket for not turning his undoubted potential into results.

But his knock in the loss means he leaves the Northern Territory as one of the only Aussie batters who can hold their heads high, with Cummins "not too sure" on the best course of action to turn things around before the second Test starts in Mackay on Saturday.

Shock loss to Bangladesh reveals Aussie cracks On paper, Australia's full-strength team should have wiped the floor with Bangladesh. But a lack of application to their Test match craft has left Australia vulnerable to teams that are driven to succeed in the longest format.

"We're always quite individual, everyone goes about it slightly differently, so coaches will work with each player individually," he said.

"I don't think there was a huge trend, everyone got out a little bit differently, but I think it's pretty clear it's not quite functioning as well as we'd like as a group.

"If we need to make some changes to our style, we've got a week or so, we better do it pretty quickly."

Cummins said before the Test that Green had been encouraged to "intimidate" and he did it the way he knows best, driving with commanding power and poise while accumulating runs at a steady rate without taking risks.

It is a method that has worked in Sheffield Shield cricket and he showcased why Test selectors have persevered with him despite the outside noise calling for his head.

Green's third Test century did not lead to a win but that was largely due to the failure of the rest of the order to stay with him in good batting conditions on the third and fourth days.

Australia will consider making changes to the underperforming top order for the second Test in Mackay that starts on Saturday, but Green will be one of the first picked.

"I'm sure he will get an extended run somewhere," Cummins said when asked if Green had tied down the number five position.

"I thought he was really impressive and controlled his innings. He looked in total command of his skills out there. He just needed one or two of us to bat alongside him."

Green and Steve Smith were the only Australian batters who could be happy with their output. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone)

Green struggled in the last Ashes series, as many batters did, making just 171 runs at an average of 24.42 after being moved around from fifth to eighth in the order.

He earlier did a solid job on the West Indies tour, averaging 30.66 at first drop as the only member of the top three to average more than 20 across the three Tests.

"We obviously think very highly of Cam," Cummins said.

"The last Ashes series probably didn't go as well as he would have liked but before that on the West Indian tour he was probably our best batter in really tough circumstances when he was batting a little higher.

"It was great for him to go out there and show the rest of the world how good he is."

Quick hits as Bangladesh wraps up famous win Litton Das was wrong-footed behind the stumps, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz suffered a worse fate in front of them. Here are the quick hits from day four of the first Test between Australia and Bangladesh.

Green was fortunate in the final session on the third day when an inside edge off Taskin Ahmed grazed his leg stump on the way to the boundary.

The bails were not dislodged and the all-rounder dug in and made the most of his reprieve.

Green told Fox Cricket after his knock that he had approached his innings against Bangladesh like he used to do "back in the day".

"I think I've just been chopping and changing a little bit recently, so it's nice just to go back to what worked," Green said.

"It has been a long couple of months so it is nice to get a few rewards for it."

As for the critics, Green said it just came with the territory.

"I feel like there are always wolves when you are playing Test cricket. When you play for Australia, you always have to perform," he said.

Tech.title: ABC’s livestreamed news show is powered by trending topics
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

ABC News has officially introduced Searched, a livestreamed show that highlights stories people are discussing on social media and searching on the web, as reported earlier by Variety. Though the network just announced the show now, Searched began airing on the ABC News Live streaming channel in April, which appears on both Disney Plus and Hulu.

In the press release, ABC News says Searched “pulls real-time data from the top search engines and social media platforms to provide topical news for the audience.” A recent episode of Searched highlighted an Illinois Powerball winner, NBA star Russell Westbrook’s retirement, and Tropical Storm Lala. You can find a backlog of episodes on the ABC News YouTube channel.

ABC News is introducing the streaming-only segment as broadcast TV viewing continues to decline, and a growing number of people turn to social media to get their news. The half-hour program is hosted by ABC News correspondents Gio Benitez and Ashan Singh, and has a new episode each weekday.

Searched will appear alongside three other new shows on ABC News Live, including All Access with Linsey Davis, featuring interviews with celebrities, politicians, athletes, and influencers; Burden of Proof, which will highlight “the most talked-about trials”; and Doctor’s Note, a series focused on highlighting medical facts and health trends.

Tech.title: This compact Glorious mechanical keyboard is just $35
Tech.content:
Brad Bourque is a tech journalist and commerce writer based out of Portland, Oregon. He’s contributed to sites like Digital Trends, Business Insider, and WIRED.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Are you curious about custom mechanical keyboards, but don’t want to spend hundreds just to get started without being sure you’ll enjoy the hobby? You can grab the 65-percent Glorious GMMK 3 mechanical keyboard at Woot for $34.99 (usually $139.99) by entering the coupon code WOOTGAMING at checkout, and first-time Woot customers will get an extra $5 off when using the same code.

It’s a well-equipped keyboard out of the box, particularly for this price, and with its support for swappable switches, it’s a great platform for exploring keycap and switch options from different makers. It’s wired only, includes a full set of double-shot PBT keycaps for both Windows and macOS, and comes with linear Glorious Fox switches pre-installed.

As a 65 percent mechanical keyboard, the layout favors just the essentials to keep a compact footprint. That means dropping the row of dedicated function keys, and limiting the extra buttons to standard modifiers, plus a couple of spare buttons for page up and down. There are still arrow keys for gaming and OS navigation, and a customizable knob for volume or media controls. Under the hood, the aluminum plate and gasket system are modifiable and upgradeable, letting you dial in the typing experience and sound.

Tech.title: Wordle meets Clippy in this new word game
Tech.content:
Like many of us, Sam Rosenthal plays games like Wordle every day, chasing after good scores and sharing the results with friends and family. But he’s also a game designer, the creative director at Blaseball developer The Game Band, and so this regular habit got him thinking about what else could be done in the space. “When I was a kid and I played word games with my family, they weren’t the New York Times puzzle games,” Rosenthal explains. “We were sitting in a car on a road trip playing these really loose games that couldn’t be made digitally before. Things like the alphabet game or our own riffs on 20 questions. That felt like a really interesting space to explore.”

This led to Dartwords, a new daily word game that launches today on the web. Dartwords is a word guessing game: Each day there’s a secret word, and you have 10 chances to figure out what it is. To start, you have no hints. You simply type in a word — any word — and from there a little Clippy-like character named Darty will respond with clues based on your guess. For instance, you might guess a type of animal, and Darty might respond saying that the answer is bigger, or maybe that it’s manmade. With each guess a dart hits a board on the screen, getting closer to the bullseye as you get closer to the right answer.

The success of Wordle has led to a deluge of daily puzzle games, particularly in the word game space, and Rosenthal says the goal of Dartwords was to create an experience that was “more conversational” compared to its contemporaries. In order to make it work, he says that the studio built a bespoke hint engine utilizing a local LLM trained on the English dictionary. He explains that Darty’s clues are a combination of broader hints generated by the LLM and, as you get closer to the correct response, clues written by the developers. “It’s this interesting mixture of using hand-authored work and local models to get us to where we want to be,” he says.

(On the subject of AI, Rosenthal says that all of the art and UI / UX in the game is handmade, while “we do use tools like Claude Code to speed up day-to-day coding tasks, but we pair them with our taste, judgment, and careful reviews.”)

Image: The Game Band

For me at least, it took a few rounds to get the hang of it. The open-ended nature of Dartwords can be almost paralyzing, as you have to try to think of a word that will get you a good hint. But eventually I started to have a better feel for how to follow up the game’s hints, and this morning I managed to get the right answer in just three guesses, a personal record. The hope is that if Dartwords becomes a success with a large player base, things will improve based on feedback and data. “Over time, with more people playing the game, our system will get better and better and hopefully serve better clues,” says Rosenthal.

Dartwords joins an increasingly eclectic lineup of games from the studio. The Game Band got its start with the narrative puzzler Where Cards Fall before launching the surreal baseball simulator Blaseball that went viral during the pandemic. More recently, the studio released Dead Man’s Party, a Knives Out-themed party game that’s part of Netflix’s current push into TV games. But with Dartwords, the studio is entering a particularly challenging and crowded space buoyed by the breakout success of Wordle. Since then, everywhere from LinkedIn to The Atlantic has started launching daily puzzle games, while platforms like Puzzmo provide their own alternative.

Rosenthal believes that one of the differentiating factors for Dartwords is Darty itself: a goofy sentient dart with big, expressive eyes and tiny hands for clapping. “Darty was literally inspired by Clippy,” he says. “The whole intent is that we wanted it to be a loose word game. It’s more improvisational, it feels more conversational. And because of that, we need something for people to get mad at if it gives you a bad clue. We want this game to feel charming and fun, and have a little more character to it than you traditionally get in word games.”

Tech.title: YouTube is changing how it counts views to give the numbers a boost
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

YouTube will soon count a view as soon as a video starts to play, lining up with the system used by Instagram, TikTok, and its Shorts videos. The update will go into effect on August 24th, “which means creators will likely see their total view counts increase faster moving forward,” the platform says.

Instagram and TikTok similarly add a view to a video when it starts to play or replay, while X counts a view when a user watches a video for at least two seconds. YouTube applied Instagram and TikTok’s view-counting method to Shorts last year.

YouTube says it’s going to keep its original view-counting method under an “engaged views” metric in its Analytics dashboard. As my colleague David Pierce notes, it’s not entirely clear how YouTube counted views before this, but “it’s generally accepted wisdom that you have to watch 30 seconds of a standard YouTube video for it to count.”

The change won’t impact creators’ earnings or how they’re eligible for the YouTube Partner Program (YPP), according to the blog post. Creator earnings will also still be based on “engaged Short views” and “engaged watch hours.”

This isn’t the only creator-related update YouTube has made lately, as the platform is also upping the requirements needed to join the YPP next year.

“Historically, we’ve used multiple view counting systems across different formats,” YouTube says in its update. “However, we’ve heard that creators want to eliminate this metric confusion and accurately understand their true exposure… We hope that having metric parity across all formats gives creators a clearer picture of their overall exposure.”
